المحاضرة 1 · ورقة مراجعة

الفصل 1: مفاهيم أمن المعلومات والشبكات

خريطة المادة كلها: ماذا نحمي (CIA)، من ماذا (الهجمات)، وبماذا (الخدمات والآليات والخوارزميات)، ولمن نثق.

01 نظرة عامة

ما موضوع المحاضرة؟

الفصل الأول من كتاب ستالينجز: مفاهيم أمن المعلومات والشبكات. يعرّف الأمن السيبراني وأمن المعلومات وأمن الشبكات، ثم الأهداف الأمنية (السرية، السلامة، الإتاحة + الأصالة والمساءلة)، ثم تحديات الأمن، ثم بنية OSI الأمنية: الهجمات (سلبية ونشطة)، والخدمات الست، والآليات الثماني. بعدها أنواع خوارزميات التشفير حسب عدد المفاتيح، وعناصر أمن الشبكات (الاتصالات والأجهزة)، وأخيرًا نموذج الثقة.

السؤال: ما الذي نحميه، ومن ماذا، وبأي أدوات؟ النطاق: 40 شريحة (اثنتان منها فارغتان).

Chapter 1 of Stallings: Information and Network Security Concepts. It defines cybersecurity, information security and network security; the security objectives (confidentiality, integrity, availability + authenticity and accountability); the challenges of security; the OSI security architecture: attacks (passive and active), the six services and the eight mechanisms; cryptographic algorithm types by number of keys; the elements of network security (communications and devices); and finally the trust model.

The question: what do we protect, against what, and with which tools? Scope: 40 slides (two of them blank).

الفكرة الأساسية

الأمن يُبنى كسلسلة: أهداف (CIA) تهددها هجمات (سلبية تُمنع، نشطة تُكشف ويُتعافى منها)، فنقدم خدمات تنفذها آليات، وأهم الآليات خوارزميات التشفير بأنواعها الثلاثة. وفوق كل ذلك الثقة بالأفراد والمنظمات والأنظمة.

Security is built as a chain: objectives (CIA) are threatened by attacks (passive ones prevented, active ones detected and recovered from), so we provide services implemented by mechanisms, the chief of which are the three kinds of cryptographic algorithm. Over all of it sits trust in people, organizations and systems.

قائمة المفاهيم الأساسية

  • الأمن السيبراني، أمن المعلومات، أمن الشبكات (3–4)
  • السرية، السلامة، الإتاحة، الأصالة، المساءلة (5–7)
  • تحديات أمن الحاسوب (8)
  • الهجوم، الخدمة، الآلية (9)
  • التهديد مقابل الهجوم (10)
  • الهجمات السلبية والنشطة (12–15)
  • الخدمات الست (16–22)
  • الآليات الثماني (23)
  • خوارزميات بلا مفتاح، مفتاح واحد، مفتاحان (24–28)
  • أمن الاتصالات وأمن الأجهزة (29–31)
  • نموذج الثقة وأنواعها (32–37)
  • Cybersecurity, information security, network security (3–4)
  • Confidentiality, integrity, availability, authenticity, accountability (5–7)
  • Computer security challenges (8)
  • Attack, service, mechanism (9)
  • Threat vs attack (10)
  • Passive and active attacks (12–15)
  • The six services (16–22)
  • The eight mechanisms (23)
  • Keyless, single-key, two-key algorithms (24–28)
  • Communications and device security (29–31)
  • Trust model and kinds of trust (32–37)

المهارات المكتسبة

  • تعريف أهداف CIA والتمييز بين فروعها (سرية البيانات/الخصوصية، سلامة البيانات/النظام).
  • تصنيف أي هجوم: سلبي أم نشط، ومن أي نوع.
  • ربط كل هجوم بالخدمة التي تواجهه والآلية التي تنفذها.
  • تصنيف الخوارزميات حسب عدد المفاتيح.
  • قراءة الأشكال 1.1–1.5.
  • التمييز بين أنواع الثقة الأربعة.
  • Define the CIA objectives and their sub-parts (data confidentiality/privacy, data/system integrity).
  • Classify an attack as passive or active, and its type.
  • Link each attack to the service that counters it and the mechanism that implements it.
  • Classify algorithms by number of keys.
  • Read Figures 1.1–1.5.
  • Distinguish the four ways of establishing trust.

لماذا يهم؟

كل فصل لاحق (التشفير الكلاسيكي، DES، التجزئة، التوقيع) هو «آلية» من الشكل 1.2 أو «خوارزمية» من الشكل 1.4. فهم هذه الخريطة يجعلك تعرف لماذا ندرس كل خوارزمية وأي هجوم تواجه.

Every later chapter (classical ciphers, DES, hashing, signatures) is a mechanism from Figure 1.2 or an algorithm from Figure 1.4. Knowing this map tells you why each algorithm is studied and which attack it counters.

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

This book focuses on two broad areas: cryptography and network security. This overview chapter first looks at some of the fundamental principles of security, encompassing both information security and network security. These include the concepts of security attacks, security services, and security mechanisms. Next, the chapter introduces the two areas of cryptography and network security. Finally, the concepts of trust and trustworthiness are examined.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Chapter 1 — Information and Network Security Concepts

    الفصل الأول: مفاهيم أمن المعلومات وأمن الشبكات، أي الأساس الذي تبنى عليه بقية المادة.

    Chapter 1: the basic concepts of information and network security that the rest of the course builds on.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

هذا الفصل لا يشرح خوارزميات بعينها، بل يعطي «الخريطة»: ما الأهداف الأمنية، ما الهجمات، ما الخدمات والآليات التي تواجهها، وما أنواع خوارزميات التشفير، وكيف نبني الثقة.

This chapter teaches no specific algorithm; it gives the map: the security objectives, the attacks, the services and mechanisms that counter them, the kinds of cryptographic algorithms, and how trust is built.

الخلاصة

الشريحة 03 — Cybersecurity

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Cybersecurity is the collection of tools, policies, security concepts, security safeguards, guidelines, risk management approaches, actions, training, best practices, assurance, and technologies that can be used to protect the cyberspace environment and organization and users’ assets. Organization and users’ assets include connected computing devices, personnel, infrastructure, applications, services, telecommunications systems, and the totality of transmitted and/or stored information in the cyberspace environment. Cybersecurity strives to ensure the attainment and maintenance of the security properties of the organization and users’ assets against relevant security risks in the cyberspace environment. The general security objectives comprise the following: availability; integrity, which may include data authenticity and nonrepudiation; and confidentiality

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

It would be useful to start this chapter with a definition of the terms cybersecurity, information security, and network security. A reasonably comprehensive definition of cybersecurity is found in ITU-T (International Telecommunication Union Telecommunication Standardization Sector) Recommendation X.1205 (Overview of Cybersecurity, 2014). Cybersecurity is the collection of tools, policies, security concepts, security safeguards, guidelines, risk management approaches, actions, training, best practices, assurance, and technologies that can be used to protect the cyberspace environment and organization and users’ assets. Organization and users’ assets include connected computing devices, personnel, infrastructure, applications, services, telecommunications systems, and the totality of transmitted and/or stored information in the cyberspace environment. Cybersecurity strives to ensure the attainment and maintenance of the security properties of the organization and users’ assets against relevant security risks in the cyberspace environment. The general security objectives comprise the following: availability; integrity, which may include data authenticity and nonrepudiation; and confidentiality.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Cybersecurity is the collection of tools, policies, security concepts, security safeguards, guidelines, risk management approaches, actions, training, best practices, assurance, and technologies that can be used to protect the cyberspace environment and organization and users’ assets.

    الأمن السيبراني مجموعة واسعة: أدوات، سياسات، مفاهيم، ضمانات، إرشادات، إدارة مخاطر، تدريب، أفضل ممارسات، وتقنيات، هدفها حماية الفضاء السيبراني وأصول المنظمة والمستخدمين.

    Cybersecurity is a broad collection (tools, policies, safeguards, risk management, training, practices, technologies) that protects cyberspace and the assets of organizations and users.

  2. Organization and users’ assets include connected computing devices, personnel, infrastructure, applications, services, telecommunications systems, and the totality of transmitted and/or stored information in the cyberspace environment.

    «الأصول» تشمل: الأجهزة المتصلة، الأفراد، البنية التحتية، التطبيقات، الخدمات، أنظمة الاتصالات، وكل المعلومات المنقولة أو المخزنة.

    “Assets” include connected devices, people, infrastructure, applications, services, telecom systems, and all transmitted or stored information.

  3. Cybersecurity strives to ensure the attainment and maintenance of the security properties of the organization and users’ assets against relevant security risks in the cyberspace environment.

    الهدف: تحقيق الخصائص الأمنية للأصول والمحافظة عليها ضد المخاطر.

    The aim: achieve and maintain the assets' security properties against relevant risks.

  4. The general security objectives comprise the following: availability; integrity, which may include data authenticity and nonrepudiation; and confidentiality

    الأهداف العامة ثلاثة: الإتاحة، السلامة (وتشمل أصالة البيانات وعدم الإنكار)، والسرية.

    The general objectives: availability; integrity (which may include authenticity and nonrepudiation); and confidentiality.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

لاحظ أن التعريف لا يقتصر على التقنية: السياسات والتدريب وإدارة المخاطر جزء منه. والأهم هو الأهداف الثلاثة في آخر جملة، وهي ما يُعرف اختصارًا بـ CIA triad (Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability)، وستُشرح في الشرائح 5–7.

The definition is not only technical: policies, training and risk management are part of it. The key part is the three objectives in the last sentence, known as the CIA triad (Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability), detailed on slides 5–7.

الخلاصة

الأمن السيبراني يحمي أصول المنظمة والمستخدمين لتحقيق: السرية، السلامة، الإتاحة.
Cybersecurity protects organizational and user assets to achieve confidentiality, integrity and availability.

الشريحة 04 — Cybersecurity — Information Security and Network Security

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Information Security
  • This term refers to preservation of confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information. In addition, other properties, such as authenticity, accountability, nonrepudiation, and reliability can also be involved
  • Network Security
  • This term refers to protection of networks and their service from unauthorized modification, destruction, or disclosure, and provision of assurance that the network performs its critical functions correctly and there are no harmful side effects

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

As subsets of cybersecurity, we can define the following: ◆  Information security: This term refers to preservation of confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information. In addition, other properties, such as authenticity, accountability, nonrepudiation, and reliability can also be involved. ◆  Network security: This term refers to protection of networks and their service from unauthorized modification, destruction, or disclosure, and provision of assurance that the network performs its critical functions correctly and there are no harmful side effects. Cybersecurity encompasses information security, with respect to electronic information, and network security. Information security also is concerned with physical (e.g., paper-based) information. However, in practice, the terms cybersecurity and information security are often used interchangeably.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Information Security — This term refers to preservation of confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information.

    أمن المعلومات: الحفاظ على سرية المعلومات وسلامتها وإتاحتها.

    Information security: preserving the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information.

  2. In addition, other properties, such as authenticity, accountability, nonrepudiation, and reliability can also be involved

    وقد يشمل خصائص إضافية: الأصالة، المساءلة، عدم الإنكار، والموثوقية.

    It may also involve authenticity, accountability, nonrepudiation and reliability.

  3. Network Security — This term refers to protection of networks and their service from unauthorized modification, destruction, or disclosure

    أمن الشبكات: حماية الشبكات وخدماتها من التعديل أو التدمير أو الكشف غير المصرح به.

    Network security: protecting networks and their services from unauthorized modification, destruction or disclosure.

  4. and provision of assurance that the network performs its critical functions correctly and there are no harmful side effects

    وضمان أن الشبكة تؤدي وظائفها الحرجة بشكل صحيح دون آثار جانبية ضارة.

    …and assuring the network performs its critical functions correctly with no harmful side effects.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

الفرق: أمن المعلومات يركز على البيانات نفسها (أينما كانت)، وأمن الشبكات يركز على الشبكة وخدماتها التي تنقل البيانات. الاثنان معًا جزء من الأمن السيبراني.

The difference: information security focuses on the data itself wherever it is; network security focuses on the network and its services that carry the data. Both are part of cybersecurity.

الخلاصة

أمن المعلومات = CIA للمعلومات (+ خصائص إضافية)؛ أمن الشبكات = حماية الشبكة وخدماتها وضمان عملها الصحيح.
Information security = CIA for information (+ extra properties); network security = protecting the network and its services and ensuring they work correctly.

الشريحة 05 — Security Objectives — Confidentiality

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • The cybersecurity definition introduces three key objectives that are at the heart of information and network security:
    • Confidentiality: This term covers two related concepts:
      • Data confidentiality: Assures that private or confidential information is not made available or disclosed to unauthorized individuals
        • Privacy: Assures that individuals control or influence what information related to them may be collected and stored and by whom and to whom that information may be disclosed

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

The cybersecurity definition introduces three key objectives that are at the heart of information and network security: ◆ Confidentiality: This term covers two related concepts: ◆ Data confidentiality: Assures that private or confidential information is not made available or disclosed to unauthorized individuals.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. The cybersecurity definition introduces three key objectives that are at the heart of information and network security:

    تعريف الأمن السيبراني يقدم ثلاثة أهداف رئيسية هي قلب أمن المعلومات والشبكات.

    The definition introduces three key objectives at the heart of information and network security.

  2. Confidentiality: This term covers two related concepts:

    السرية تشمل مفهومين مترابطين.

    Confidentiality covers two related concepts.

  3. Data confidentiality: Assures that private or confidential information is not made available or disclosed to unauthorized individuals

    سرية البيانات: المعلومات الخاصة لا تُكشف لغير المصرح لهم.

    Data confidentiality: private information is not disclosed to unauthorized individuals.

  4. Privacy: Assures that individuals control or influence what information related to them may be collected and stored and by whom and to whom that information may be disclosed

    الخصوصية: الفرد يتحكم في ما يُجمع ويُخزن عنه، ومن يجمعه، ولمن يُكشف.

    Privacy: individuals control what is collected and stored about them, by whom, and to whom it is disclosed.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

الفرق الدقيق: سرية البيانات تحمي البيانات من الأشخاص غير المصرح لهم، أما الخصوصية فتعطي الشخص حق التحكم في بياناته. مثال: مستشفى يحفظ ملفك مشفرًا (سرية)، لكن الخصوصية تعني أن لك رأيًا في مشاركته مع شركة تأمين.

The subtle difference: data confidentiality protects data from unauthorized people; privacy gives the person control over their data. Example: a hospital keeps your file encrypted (confidentiality), but privacy means you have a say in sharing it with an insurer.

الخلاصة

السرية = سرية البيانات + الخصوصية.
Confidentiality = data confidentiality + privacy.

الشريحة 06 — Security Objectives — Integrity and Availability

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Integrity: This term covers two related concepts:
    • Data integrity: Assures that data and programs are changed only in a specified and authorized manner. This concept also encompasses data authenticity, which means that a digital object is indeed what it claims to be or what it is claimed to be, and nonrepudiation, which is assurance that the sender of information is provided with proof of delivery and the recipient is provided with proof of the sender’s identity, so neither can later deny having processed the information
    • System integrity: Assures that a system performs its intended function in an unimpaired manner, free from deliberate or inadvertent unauthorized manipulation of the system
  • Availability: Assures that systems work promptly and service is not denied to authorized users

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

◆  Integrity: This term covers two related concepts: ◆ Data integrity: Assures that data (both stored and in transmitted packets) and programs are changed only in a specified and authorized manner. This concept also encompasses data authenticity, which means that a digital object is indeed what it claims to be or what it is claimed to be, and nonrepudiation, which is assurance that the sender of information is provided with proof of delivery and the recipient is provided with proof of the sender’s identity, so neither can later deny having processed the information. ◆ System integrity: Assures that a system performs its intended function in an unimpaired manner, free from deliberate or inadvertent unauthorized manipulation of the system.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Integrity: This term covers two related concepts:

    السلامة تشمل مفهومين.

    Integrity covers two concepts.

  2. Data integrity: Assures that data and programs are changed only in a specified and authorized manner.

    سلامة البيانات: البيانات والبرامج لا تتغير إلا بطريقة محددة ومصرح بها.

    Data integrity: data and programs change only in a specified, authorized way.

  3. This concept also encompasses data authenticity, which means that a digital object is indeed what it claims to be or what it is claimed to be

    وتشمل أصالة البيانات: الكائن الرقمي هو فعلًا ما يدّعي أنه هو.

    It includes data authenticity: a digital object really is what it claims to be.

  4. and nonrepudiation, which is assurance that the sender of information is provided with proof of delivery and the recipient is provided with proof of the sender’s identity, so neither can later deny having processed the information

    وعدم الإنكار: المرسل يحصل على إثبات التسليم، والمستلم يحصل على إثبات هوية المرسل، فلا يستطيع أي منهما الإنكار لاحقًا.

    And nonrepudiation: the sender gets proof of delivery and the recipient gets proof of the sender's identity, so neither can later deny it.

  5. System integrity: Assures that a system performs its intended function in an unimpaired manner, free from deliberate or inadvertent unauthorized manipulation of the system

    سلامة النظام: النظام يؤدي وظيفته المقصودة دون تلاعب، متعمد أو غير متعمد.

    System integrity: the system performs its intended function free from deliberate or accidental unauthorized manipulation.

  6. Availability: Assures that systems work promptly and service is not denied to authorized users

    الإتاحة: الأنظمة تعمل بسرعة ولا تُمنع الخدمة عن المستخدمين المصرح لهم.

    Availability: systems work promptly and service is not denied to authorized users.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

سلامة البيانات تخص المحتوى، وسلامة النظام تخص السلوك. مثال: تغيير مبلغ تحويل بنكي = خرق سلامة بيانات؛ برنامج خبيث يجعل الخادم يحسب الفوائد خطأ = خرق سلامة نظام. والإتاحة تُخرق بهجمات حجب الخدمة (DoS).

Data integrity concerns content; system integrity concerns behaviour. Changing a bank transfer amount breaks data integrity; malware making a server compute interest wrongly breaks system integrity. Availability is broken by denial-of-service attacks.

الخلاصة

السلامة = سلامة البيانات (+ الأصالة وعدم الإنكار) + سلامة النظام؛ الإتاحة = الخدمة متاحة للمصرح لهم.
Integrity = data integrity (+ authenticity, nonrepudiation) + system integrity; availability = service available to authorized users.

مخمس منتظم. في وسطه مخمس أسود مكتوب عليه بالأبيض «أمن المعلومات والشبكات». حوله خمسة أشرطة ملونة تشكل أضلاع المخمس الخارجي، كل شريط هدف أمني: أعلى اليسار أخضر «السرية (مع الخصوصية)»، أعلى اليمين بنفسجي «السلامة (مع أصالة البيانات وعدم الإنكار)»، اليمين برتقالي وردي «الأصالة»، الأسفل أزرق فاتح «الإتاحة»، اليسار أصفر «المساءلة». المعنى: هذه الأهداف الخمسة تحيط بأمن المعلومات وتحدده.
A regular pentagon. In the middle, a black pentagon reading “Information and Network Security” in white. Around it, five coloured bands form the outer sides, each an objective: top-left green “Confidentiality (plus privacy)”, top-right purple “Integrity (plus data authenticity, non-repudiation)”, right orange-pink “Authenticity”, bottom light-blue “Availability”, left yellow “Accountability”. Meaning: these five objectives surround and define information security.

ترتيب القراءة

  1. ابدأ بالمركز: أمن المعلومات والشبكات.
  2. ثم الأضلاع باتجاه عقارب الساعة من أعلى اليسار: السرية، السلامة، الأصالة، الإتاحة، المساءلة.
  1. Start at the centre: Information and Network Security.
  2. Then the sides clockwise from top-left: Confidentiality, Integrity, Authenticity, Availability, Accountability.

مخطط معاد بناؤه

              Confidentiality (plus privacy)
   Accountability   [ Information and   ]   Integrity (plus data authenticity,
                    [ Network Security  ]              non-repudiation)
                 Availability          Authenticity
📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

These three concepts form what is often referred to as the CIA triad. The three concepts embody the fundamental security objectives for both data and for information and computing services. For example, the NIST standard FIPS 199 (Standards for Security Categorization of Federal Information and Information Systems ) lists confidentiality, integrity, and availability as the three security objectives for information and for information systems. FIPS 199 provides a useful characterization of these three objectives in terms of requirements and the definition of a loss of security in each category: • Confidentiality: Preserving authorized restrictions on information access and disclosure, including means for protecting personal privacy and proprietary information. A loss of confidentiality is the unauthorized disclosure of information. • Integrity: Guarding against improper information modification or destruction, including ensuring information nonrepudiation and authenticity. A loss of integrity is the unauthorized modification or destruction of information. • Availability: Ensuring timely and reliable access to and use of information. A loss of availability is the disruption of access to or use of information or an information system. Although the use of the CIA triad to define security objectives is well established, some in the security field feel that additional concepts are needed to present a complete picture (Figure 1.1). Two of the most commonly mentioned are as follows: • Authenticity: The property of being genuine and being able to be verified and trusted; confidence in the validity of a transmission, a message, or message originator. This means verifying that users are who they say they are and that each input arriving at the system came from a trusted source. • Accountability: The security goal that generates the requirement for actions of an entity to be traced uniquely to that entity. This supports nonrepudiation, deterrence, fault isolation, intrusion detection and prevention, and after action recovery and legal action. Because truly secure systems are not yet an achievable goal, we must be able to trace a security breach to a responsible party. Systems must keep records of their activities to permit later forensic analysis to trace security breaches or to aid in transaction disputes.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Figure 1.1 Essential Information and Network Security Objectives

    الشكل يجمع الأهداف الثلاثة (CIA) مع هدفين إضافيين: الأصالة والمساءلة.

    The figure combines the three CIA objectives with two more: authenticity and accountability.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

الأصالة Authenticity: التحقق من أن المستخدم أو المصدر هو من يدّعي. المساءلة Accountability: إمكانية تتبع أي فعل إلى الشخص الذي قام به (سجلات، تدقيق). ملاحظات الشريحة في الكتاب تشرح هذين الهدفين بهذا المعنى.

Authenticity: verifying that a user or source is who it claims to be. Accountability: being able to trace any action to whoever performed it (logs, audit). The slide notes from the book describe both this way.

الخلاصة

خمسة أهداف أمنية: السرية، السلامة، الإتاحة، الأصالة، المساءلة.
Five security objectives: confidentiality, integrity, availability, authenticity, accountability.

الشريحة 08 — Computer Security Challenges

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Security is not simple
  • Potential attacks on the security features need to be considered
  • Procedures used to provide particular services are often counter-intuitive
  • It is necessary to decide where to use the various security mechanisms
  • Requires constant monitoring
  • Is too often an afterthought
  • Security mechanisms typically involve more than a particular algorithm or protocol
  • Security is essentially a battle of wits between a perpetrator and the designer
  • Little benefit from security investment is perceived until a security failure occurs
  • Strong security is often viewed as an impediment to efficient and user-friendly operation

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Computer and network security is both fascinating and complex. Some of the reasons follow: 1. Security is not as simple as it might first appear to the novice. The requirements seem to be straightforward; indeed, most of the major requirements for security services can be given self-explanatory, one-word labels: confidentiality, authentication, nonrepudiation, or integrity. But the mechanisms used to meet those requirements can be quite complex, and understanding them may involve rather subtle reasoning. 2. In developing a particular security mechanism or algorithm, one must always consider potential attacks on those security features. In many cases, successful attacks are designed by looking at the problem in a completely different way, therefore exploiting an unexpected weakness in the mechanism. 3. Because of point 2, the procedures used to provide particular services are often counterintuitive. Typically, a security mechanism is complex, and it is not obvious from the statement of a particular requirement that such elaborate measures are needed. It is only when the various aspects of the threat are considered that elaborate security mechanisms make sense. 4. Having designed various security mechanisms, it is necessary to decide where to use them. This is true both in terms of physical placement (e.g., at what points in a network are certain security mechanisms needed) and in a logical sense (e.g., at what layer or layers of an architecture such as TCP/IP [Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol] should mechanisms be placed). 5. Security mechanisms typically involve more than a particular algorithm or protocol. They also require that participants be in possession of some secret information (e.g., an encryption key), which raises questions about the creation, distribution, and protection of that secret information. There also may be a reliance on communications protocols whose behavior may complicate the task of developing the security mechanism. For example, if the proper functioning of the security mechanism requires setting time limits on the transit time of a message from sender to receiver, then any protocol or network that introduces variable, unpredictable delays may render such time limits meaningless. 6. Computer and network security is essentially a battle of wits between a perpetrator who tries to find holes and the designer or administrator who tries to close them. The great advantage that the attacker has is that he or she need only find a single weakness, while the designer must find and eliminate all weaknesses to achieve perfect security. 7. There is a natural tendency on the part of users and system managers to perceive little benefit from security investment until a security failure occurs. 8. Security requires regular, even constant, monitoring, and this is difficult in today’s short-term, overloaded environment. 9. Security is still too often an afterthought to be incorporated into a system after the design is complete rather than being an integral part of the design process. 10. Many users and even security administrators view strong security as an impediment to efficient and user-friendly operation of an information system or use of information.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Security is not simple

    الأمن ليس بسيطًا: المتطلبات تبدو سهلة لكن تحقيقها معقد.

    Security is not simple: requirements look easy but are hard to meet.

  2. Potential attacks on the security features need to be considered

    يجب التفكير في الهجمات المحتملة على آليات الأمن نفسها.

    Attacks on the security features themselves must be considered.

  3. Procedures used to provide particular services are often counter-intuitive

    الإجراءات المستخدمة غالبًا غير بديهية (لا تتضح أسبابها إلا بعد فهم التهديدات).

    Procedures are often counter-intuitive (their reasons only make sense once the threats are understood).

  4. It is necessary to decide where to use the various security mechanisms

    يجب تحديد أين توضع آليات الأمن (في أي نقطة من الشبكة أو أي طبقة).

    You must decide where to place the mechanisms (which point in the network, which layer).

  5. Requires constant monitoring

    يتطلب مراقبة مستمرة.

    Requires constant monitoring.

  6. Is too often an afterthought

    كثيرًا ما يُضاف الأمن في النهاية بدل أن يُصمم من البداية.

    Too often added at the end instead of designed in.

  7. Security mechanisms typically involve more than a particular algorithm or protocol

    الآلية الأمنية أكثر من خوارزمية: تحتاج مثلًا مفاتيح سرية يجب توزيعها وحمايتها.

    A mechanism is more than an algorithm: e.g. it needs secret keys that must be distributed and protected.

  8. Security is essentially a battle of wits between a perpetrator and the designer

    الأمن معركة ذكاء بين المهاجم والمصمم: المهاجم يكفيه ثغرة واحدة، والمصمم يجب أن يسد كل الثغرات.

    Security is a battle of wits: the attacker needs one hole; the designer must close them all.

  9. Little benefit from security investment is perceived until a security failure occurs

    لا تُرى فائدة الاستثمار في الأمن حتى يحدث اختراق.

    The value of security investment is rarely seen until a failure happens.

  10. Strong security is often viewed as an impediment to efficient and user-friendly operation

    الأمن القوي يُنظر إليه كعائق أمام سهولة الاستخدام والكفاءة.

    Strong security is often seen as getting in the way of efficiency and usability.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

هذه عشرة تحديات، ويمكن تجميعها في ثلاث مجموعات: تقنية (التعقيد، الهجمات على الآليات، أين نضع الآليات، الآلية أكثر من خوارزمية)، إدارية (المراقبة المستمرة، الأمن كفكرة لاحقة، صعوبة إثبات قيمة الاستثمار)، وبشرية (معركة الذكاء، تعارض الأمن مع سهولة الاستخدام).

Ten challenges, which group into three: technical (complexity, attacks on mechanisms, placement, more than an algorithm), managerial (constant monitoring, afterthought, hard-to-see return on investment) and human (battle of wits, conflict with usability).

الخلاصة

الأمن صعب تقنيًا وإداريًا وبشريًا؛ عشرة تحديات.
Security is hard technically, managerially and humanly; ten challenges.

الشريحة 09 — OSI Security Architecture

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Security attack
  • Any action that compromises the security of information owned by an organization
  • Security mechanism
  • A process (or a device incorporating such a process) that is designed to detect, prevent, or recover from a security attack
  • Security service
  • A processing or communication service that enhances the security of the data processing systems and the information transfers of an organization
  • Intended to counter security attacks, and they make use of one or more security mechanisms to provide the service

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

To assess effectively the security needs of an organization and to evaluate and choose various security products and policies, the manager responsible for security needs some systematic way of defining the requirements for security and characterizing the approaches to satisfying those requirements. This is difficult enough in a centralized data processing environment; with the use of local and wide area networks, the problems are compounded. ITU-T Recommendation X.800, Security Architecture for OSI, defines such a systematic approach. The OSI security architecture is useful to managers as a way of organizing the task of providing security. Furthermore, because this architecture was developed as an international standard, computer and communications vendors have developed security features for their products and services that relate to this structured definition of services and mechanisms. For our purposes, the OSI security architecture provides a useful, if abstract, overview of many of the concepts that this book deals with. The OSI security architecture focuses on security attacks, mechanisms, and services. These can be defined briefly as • Security attack: Any action that compromises the security of information owned by an organization. • Security mechanism: A process (or a device incorporating such a process) that is designed to detect, prevent, or recover from a security attack. • Security service: A processing or communication service that enhances the security of the data processing systems and the information transfers of an organization. The services are intended to counter security attacks, and they make use of one or more security mechanisms to provide the service.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Security attack — Any action that compromises the security of information owned by an organization

    الهجوم الأمني: أي فعل يضر بأمن معلومات المنظمة.

    Security attack: any action that compromises the security of an organization's information.

  2. Security mechanism — A process (or a device incorporating such a process) that is designed to detect, prevent, or recover from a security attack

    الآلية الأمنية: عملية (أو جهاز) مصممة لكشف الهجوم أو منعه أو التعافي منه.

    Security mechanism: a process (or device) designed to detect, prevent or recover from an attack.

  3. Security service — A processing or communication service that enhances the security of the data processing systems and the information transfers of an organization

    الخدمة الأمنية: خدمة تعزز أمن أنظمة المعالجة ونقل المعلومات.

    Security service: a service that enhances the security of processing systems and information transfers.

  4. Intended to counter security attacks, and they make use of one or more security mechanisms to provide the service

    الخدمات تواجه الهجمات، وتستخدم آلية أو أكثر لتقديم الخدمة.

    Services counter attacks and use one or more mechanisms to do so.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

العلاقة بين الثلاثة: الهجوم هو المشكلة، والخدمة هي «ماذا نريد» لمواجهته (مثل السرية)، والآلية هي «كيف» نحقق الخدمة (مثل التشفير). مثال: هجوم تنصت ← خدمة سرية البيانات ← آلية التشفير.

Attack  --countered by-->  Service  --implemented by-->  Mechanism(s)
eavesdropping            data confidentiality          encryption

How they relate: the attack is the problem, the service is “what” we want against it (e.g. confidentiality), and the mechanism is “how” we deliver the service (e.g. encryption).

Attack  --countered by-->  Service  --implemented by-->  Mechanism(s)
eavesdropping            data confidentiality          encryption

الخلاصة

بنية OSI الأمنية: هجوم ← خدمة تواجهه ← آلية تنفذ الخدمة.
OSI security architecture: attack → service that counters it → mechanism that implements the service.

الشريحة 10 — Threats and Attacks

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

[No text on this slide other than the figure and the copyright footer.]

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

المصدر — النص داخل الصورة

Threat
A potential for violation of security, which exists when there is a circumstance, capability, action, or event that could breach security and cause harm. That is, a threat is a possible danger that might exploit a vulnerability.

Attack
An assault on system security that derives from an intelligent threat; that is, an intelligent act that is a deliberate attempt (especially in the sense of a method or technique) to evade security services and violate the security policy of a system.

🖼 إظهار وصف الإتاحة

إتاحة — وصف الصورة

مربع رمادي فاتح بإطار أسود، فيه فقرتان. الأولى عنوانها بالخط العريض «Threat» وتحتها التعريف، والثانية «Attack» وتحتها التعريف.
A light-grey box with a black border containing two paragraphs: the bold heading “Threat” with its definition, then the bold heading “Attack” with its definition.
📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

In the literature, the terms threat and attack are commonly used, with the following meanings: ■ Threat: Any circumstance or event with the potential to adversely impact organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, or the Nation through an information system via unauthorized access, destruction, disclosure, modification of information, and/or denial of service. ■. Attack: Any kind of malicious activity that attempts to collect, disrupt, deny, degrade, or destroy information system resources or the information itself.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Threat — A potential for violation of security … a threat is a possible danger that might exploit a vulnerability.

    التهديد: احتمال خرق الأمن؛ خطر ممكن قد يستغل ثغرة.

    Threat: a potential for a security violation; a possible danger that might exploit a vulnerability.

  2. Attack — An assault on system security that derives from an intelligent threat … a deliberate attempt … to evade security services and violate the security policy of a system.

    الهجوم: اعتداء فعلي ومتعمد ناتج عن تهديد ذكي، يحاول تجاوز الخدمات الأمنية وخرق سياسة النظام.

    Attack: an actual, deliberate assault from an intelligent threat, trying to evade security services and violate the system's policy.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

التهديد = احتمال، الهجوم = فعل. مثال: وجود ثغرة في برنامج غير محدَّث هو تهديد؛ قيام شخص باستغلالها فعلًا هو هجوم. الصورة الثانية (جرس إنذار مكتوب تحته Danger!) زخرفية.

Threat = possibility; attack = action. An unpatched vulnerability is a threat; someone actually exploiting it is an attack. The second image (an alarm bell with “Danger!” below) is decorative.

الخلاصة

التهديد خطر محتمل؛ الهجوم محاولة متعمدة فعلية.
A threat is a potential danger; an attack is an actual deliberate attempt.

الشريحة 12 — Security Attacks

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • A means of classifying security attacks, used both in X.800 and RFC 4949, is in terms of passive attacks and active attacks
  • A passive attack attempts to learn or make use of information from the system but does not affect system resources

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

A useful means of classifying security attacks, used both in X.800, is in terms of passive attacks and active attacks (Figure 1.2a). A passive attack attempts to learn or make use of information from the system but does not affect system resources. An active attack attempts to alter system resources or affect their operation.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. A means of classifying security attacks, used both in X.800 and RFC 4949, is in terms of passive attacks and active attacks

    تصنيف الهجمات في معياري X.800 وRFC 4949: سلبية ونشطة.

    X.800 and RFC 4949 classify attacks as passive or active.

  2. A passive attack attempts to learn or make use of information from the system but does not affect system resources

    الهجوم السلبي يحاول معرفة المعلومات أو استخدامها دون التأثير على موارد النظام.

    A passive attack tries to learn or use information without affecting system resources.

  3. An active attack attempts to alter system resources or affect their operation

    الهجوم النشط يحاول تغيير موارد النظام أو التأثير على عملها.

    An active attack tries to alter system resources or affect their operation.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

الكلمة المفتاحية: هل يغيّر المهاجم شيئًا؟ لا ← سلبي (يسمع فقط). نعم ← نشط. لهذا الهجوم السلبي صعب الكشف لأنه لا يترك أثرًا.

The key question: does the attacker change anything? No → passive (only listens). Yes → active. That is why passive attacks are hard to detect: they leave no trace.

الخلاصة

سلبي = يتعلم دون تغيير؛ نشط = يغيّر أو يعطّل.
Passive = learns without changing; active = alters or disrupts.

الشريحة 13 — Passive Attacks

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Two types of passive attacks are:
    • The release of message contents
    • Traffic analysis
  • Are in the nature of eavesdropping on, or monitoring of, transmissions
  • Goal of the opponent is to obtain information that is being transmitted

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Passive attacks are in the nature of eavesdropping on, or monitoring of, transmissions. The goal of the opponent is to obtain information that is being transmitted. Two types of passive attacks are the release of message contents and traffic analysis. The release of message contents is easily understood. A telephone conversation, an electronic mail message, and a transferred file may contain sensitive or confidential information. We would like to prevent an opponent from learning the contents of these transmissions. A second type of passive attack, traffic analysis, is subtler. Suppose that we had a way of masking the contents of messages or other information traffic so that opponents, even if they captured the message, could not extract the information from the message. The common technique for masking contents is encryption. If we had encryption protection in place, an opponent might still be able to observe the pattern of these messages. The opponent could determine the location and identity of communicating hosts and could observe the frequency and length of messages being exchanged. This information might be useful in guessing the nature of the communication that was taking place. Passive attacks are very difficult to detect, because they do not involve any alteration of the data. Typically, the message traffic is sent and received in an apparently normal fashion, and neither the sender nor receiver is aware that a third party has read the messages or observed the traffic pattern. However, it is feasible to prevent the success of these attacks, usually by means of encryption. Thus, the emphasis in dealing with passive attacks is on prevention rather than detection.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Two types of passive attacks are: The release of message contents / Traffic analysis

    نوعان: كشف محتوى الرسالة (قراءة ما فيها)، وتحليل حركة المرور (مراقبة من يتواصل مع من، ومتى، وكم).

    Two types: release of message contents (reading it) and traffic analysis (observing who talks to whom, when, how much).

  2. Are in the nature of eavesdropping on, or monitoring of, transmissions

    طبيعتها تنصت أو مراقبة للإرسال.

    They are eavesdropping or monitoring of transmissions.

  3. Goal of the opponent is to obtain information that is being transmitted

    هدف الخصم: الحصول على المعلومات المنقولة.

    The opponent's goal is to obtain the transmitted information.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

تحليل حركة المرور يعمل حتى لو كانت الرسائل مشفرة: المهاجم لا يقرأ المحتوى، لكنه يرى المصدر والوجهة والتكرار والطول، ويستنتج منها (مثلًا: زيادة الرسائل بين جهتين قبل حدث مهم). الصورة (رجل يضع كوبًا على أذنه ليتنصت) زخرفية وتوضح فكرة التنصت. الحماية من الهجمات السلبية تكون بـالمنع (كالتشفير) لا بالكشف.

Traffic analysis works even on encrypted messages: the attacker can't read content but sees source, destination, frequency and length, and infers from them (e.g. more messages between two parties before a big event). The image (a man pressing a cup to his ear to eavesdrop) is decorative. Passive attacks are handled by prevention (e.g. encryption), not detection.

الخلاصة

الهجمات السلبية: كشف المحتوى وتحليل المرور؛ تنصت بلا تغيير.
Passive attacks: release of contents and traffic analysis; eavesdropping without change.

الشريحة 14 — Active Attacks

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Involve some modification of the data stream or the creation of a false stream
  • Difficult to prevent because of the wide variety of potential physical, software, and network vulnerabilities
  • Goal is to detect attacks and to recover from any disruption or delays caused by them
Four active-attack boxes on the right of the slide (label → description)
MasqueradeTakes place when one entity pretends to be a different entity
Usually includes one of the other forms of active attack
ReplayInvolves the passive capture of a data unit and its subsequent retransmission to produce an unauthorized effect
Data ModificationSome portion of a legitimate message is altered, or messages are delayed or reordered to produce an unauthorized effect
Denial of servicePrevents or inhibits the normal use or management of communications facilities

[Layout reconstructed from shape positions: each label box sits to the left of its description box.]

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Active attacks involve some modification of the data stream or the creation of a false stream and can be subdivided into four categories: masquerade, replay, modification of messages, and denial of service. A masquerade takes place when one entity pretends to be a different entity. A masquerade attack usually includes one of the other forms of active attack. For example, authentication sequences can be captured and replayed after a valid authentication sequence has taken place, thus enabling an authorized entity with few privileges to obtain extra privileges by impersonating an entity that has those privileges. Replay involves the passive capture of a data unit and its subsequent retransmission to produce an unauthorized effect. Data modification simply means that some portion of a legitimate message is altered, or that messages are delayed or reordered, to produce an unauthorized effect. For example, a message stating, “Allow John Smith to read confidential file accounts” is modified to say, “Allow Fred Brown to read confidential file accounts.” The denial of service prevents or inhibits the normal use or management of communications facilities. This attack may have a specific target; for example, an entity may suppress all messages directed to a particular destination (e.g., the security audit service). Another form of service denial is the disruption of an entire network, either by disabling the network or by overloading it with messages so as to degrade performance. Active attacks present the opposite characteristics of passive attacks. Whereas passive attacks are difficult to detect, measures are available to prevent their success. On the other hand, it is quite difficult to prevent active attacks absolutely because of the wide variety of potential physical, software, and network vulnerabilities. Instead, the goal is to detect active attacks and to recover from any disruption or delays caused by them. If the detection has a deterrent effect, it may also contribute to prevention.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Involve some modification of the data stream or the creation of a false stream

    الهجمات النشطة تعدّل تدفق البيانات أو تنشئ تدفقًا مزيفًا.

    Active attacks modify the data stream or create a false one.

  2. Difficult to prevent because of the wide variety of potential physical, software, and network vulnerabilities

    يصعب منعها لكثرة الثغرات المحتملة (مادية، برمجية، شبكية).

    Hard to prevent because of the many possible physical, software and network vulnerabilities.

  3. Goal is to detect attacks and to recover from any disruption or delays caused by them

    لذلك الهدف هو الكشف والتعافي، عكس الهجمات السلبية التي نهدف لمنعها.

    So the goal is detection and recovery, unlike passive attacks, which we aim to prevent.

  4. Masquerade — one entity pretends to be a different entity

    انتحال الشخصية: كيان يتظاهر بأنه كيان آخر، وغالبًا يتضمن نوعًا آخر من الهجمات النشطة (مثل إعادة إرسال بيانات تسجيل دخول).

    Masquerade: one entity pretends to be another, usually combined with another active attack (e.g. replaying login data).

  5. Replay — passive capture of a data unit and its subsequent retransmission

    إعادة الإرسال: التقاط بيانات ثم إعادة إرسالها لاحقًا لإحداث أثر غير مصرح به.

    Replay: capture a data unit, then resend it later for an unauthorized effect.

  6. Data Modification — a portion of a legitimate message is altered, or messages are delayed or reordered

    تعديل البيانات: تغيير جزء من رسالة شرعية أو تأخير الرسائل أو تغيير ترتيبها.

    Data modification: altering part of a legitimate message, or delaying or reordering messages.

  7. Denial of service — prevents or inhibits the normal use or management of communications facilities

    حجب الخدمة: منع الاستخدام الطبيعي لمرافق الاتصال أو إدارتها.

    Denial of service: preventing normal use or management of communication facilities.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

مثال لكل نوع: انتحال: مهاجم يرسل بريدًا وكأنه المدير. إعادة إرسال: التقاط أمر «حوّل 100$» وإرساله مرة أخرى. تعديل: تغيير «اسمح لأحمد» إلى «اسمح لفلان». حجب الخدمة: إغراق الخادم بطلبات حتى يتوقف. الصورة (نمر يتهيأ للانقضاض) زخرفية.

One example each: masquerade: an attacker emails pretending to be the boss. Replay: capturing a “transfer $100” order and sending it again. Modification: changing “allow Ahmed” to “allow someone else”. Denial of service: flooding a server until it stops. The image (a tiger about to pounce) is decorative.

الخلاصة

4 هجمات نشطة: انتحال، إعادة إرسال، تعديل، حجب خدمة؛ الهدف كشفها والتعافي.
4 active attacks: masquerade, replay, modification, DoS; the goal is detection and recovery.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Figure 1.3 illustrates the types of attacks in the context of a client/server interaction. A passive attack (Figure 1.3b) does not disturb the information flow between the client and server, but is able to observe that flow. A masquerade can take the form of a man-in-the-middle attack (Figure 1.3c). In this type of attack, the attacker intercepts masquerades as the client to the server and as the server to the client. We see specific applications of this attack in defeating key exchange and distribution protocols (Chapters 10 and 14) and in message authentication protocols (Chapter 11). More generally, it can be used to impersonate the two ends of a legitimate communication. Another form of masquerade is illustrated in Figure 1.3d. Here, an attacker is able to access server resources by masquerading as an authorized user. Data modification may involve a man-in-the middle attack, in which the attacker selectively modifies communicated data between a client and server (Figure 1.3c). Another form of data modification attack is the modification of data residing on a serve or other system after an attacker gains unauthorized access (Figure 1.3d). Figure 1.3e illustrates the replay attack. As in a passive attack, the attacker does not disturb the information flow between client and server, but does capture client message. The attacker can then subsequently replay any client message to the server. Figure 1.3d also illustrates denial of service in the context of a client/server environment. The denial of service can take two forms: (1) flooding the server with an overwhelming amount of data; and (2) triggering some action on the server that consumes substantial computing resources.

  2. (b) Passive attack (eavesdrop, traffic analysis)

    المهاجم يستمع فقط (سهم متقطع) ولا يغيّر شيئًا.

    The attacker only listens (dashed arrow) and changes nothing.

  3. (c) Active attack (masquerade, data modification)

    المهاجم في المنتصف: يستقبل من الطرفين ويرسل لهما، فيمكنه التعديل أو الانتحال.

    The attacker sits in the middle, receiving and sending to both sides, so can modify or impersonate.

  4. (d) Active attack (masquerade, data modification, denial of service)

    المهاجم يتصل بالخادم مباشرة (منتحلًا العميل) أو يغرقه فيحجب الخدمة.

    The attacker connects to the server directly (pretending to be the client) or floods it.

  5. (e) Active attack (replay)

    المهاجم يلتقط الرسائل (متقطع) ثم يعيد إرسالها للخادم (صلب).

    The attacker captures messages (dashed) and resends them to the server (solid).

الشريحة 16 — Authentication

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Concerned with assuring that a communication is authentic
    • In the case of a single message, assures the recipient that the message is from the source that it claims to be from
      • In the case of ongoing interaction, assures the two entities are authentic and that the connection is not interfered with in such a way that a third party can masquerade as one of the two legitimate parties
  • Two specific authentication services are defined in X.800:
  • Peer entity authentication
  • Data origin authentication

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

The authentication service is concerned with assuring that a communication is authentic. In the case of a single message, such as a warning or alarm signal, the function of the authentication service is to assure the recipient that the message is from the source that it claims to be from. In the case of an ongoing interaction, such as the connection of a terminal to a host, two aspects are involved. First, at the time of connection initiation, the service assures that the two entities are authentic, that is, that each is the entity that it claims to be. Second, the service must assure that the connection is not interfered with in such a way that a third party can masquerade as one of the two legitimate parties for the purposes of unauthorized transmission or reception. Two specific authentication services are defined in X.800: • Peer entity authentication: Provides for the corroboration of the identity of a peer entity in an association. Two entities are considered peers if they implement to same protocol in different systems; for example two TCP modules in two communicating systems. Peer entity authentication is provided for use at the establishment of, or at times during the data transfer phase of, a connection. It attempts to provide confidence that an entity is not performing either a masquerade or an unauthorized replay of a previous connection. • Data origin authentication: Provides for the corroboration of the source of a data unit. It does not provide protection against the duplication or modification of data units. This type of service supports applications like electronic mail, where there are no prior interactions between the communicating entities.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Concerned with assuring that a communication is authentic

    خدمة المصادقة تضمن أن الاتصال أصيل (حقيقي).

    Authentication assures that a communication is authentic.

  2. In the case of a single message, assures the recipient that the message is from the source that it claims to be from

    لرسالة واحدة: تؤكد للمستلم أن الرسالة من المصدر الذي تدّعيه.

    For a single message: assures the recipient that it comes from the claimed source.

  3. In the case of ongoing interaction, assures the two entities are authentic and that the connection is not interfered with in such a way that a third party can masquerade as one of the two legitimate parties

    لاتصال مستمر: تؤكد أن الطرفين حقيقيان، وأن طرفًا ثالثًا لا يستطيع التدخل وانتحال أحدهما.

    For ongoing interaction: assures both entities are authentic and no third party can interfere and masquerade as one of them.

  4. Two specific authentication services are defined in X.800: Peer entity authentication / Data origin authentication

    X.800 يعرّف نوعين: مصادقة الكيان النظير، ومصادقة مصدر البيانات.

    X.800 defines two: peer entity authentication and data origin authentication.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

المصادقة هي الخدمة التي تواجه هجوم الانتحال (الشريحة 14) مباشرة.

Authentication is the service that directly counters masquerade (slide 14).

الخلاصة

المصادقة تضمن أصالة المصدر؛ نوعان: الكيان النظير، ومصدر البيانات.
Authentication assures the source is genuine; two kinds: peer entity and data origin.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

In the context of network security, access control is the ability to limit and control the access to host systems and applications via communications links. To achieve this, each entity trying to gain access must first be identified, or authenticated, so that access rights can be tailored to the individual.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. The ability to limit and control the access to host systems and applications via communications links

    التحكم في الوصول: القدرة على تقييد الوصول إلى الأنظمة والتطبيقات عبر الشبكة.

    Access control: the ability to limit and control access to systems and applications over communication links.

  2. To achieve this, each entity trying to gain access must first be indentified, or authenticated, so that access rights can be tailored to the individual

    لتحقيقه يجب أولًا تحديد هوية كل كيان أو مصادقته، ثم تُعطى له صلاحيات مناسبة. (كلمة indentified في الشريحة خطأ مطبعي لـ identified.)

    To do this, each entity must first be identified or authenticated, so access rights can be tailored. (“indentified” on the slide is a typo for “identified”.)

الشرح — شرح موسّع

ترتيب منطقي: المصادقة أولًا (من أنت؟) ثم التحكم في الوصول (ماذا يُسمح لك؟). الصورة (رجل أمام حاسوب عليه علامة «ممنوع») زخرفية.

Logical order: authentication first (who are you?), then access control (what are you allowed?). The image (a man facing a computer showing a “no entry” sign) is decorative.

الخلاصة

التحكم في الوصول يعتمد على المصادقة لتحديد الصلاحيات.
Access control relies on authentication to tailor permissions.

الشريحة 19 — Data Confidentiality

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • The protection of transmitted data from passive attacks
    • Broadest service protects all user data transmitted between two users over a period of time
      • Narrower forms of service includes the protection of a single message or even specific fields within a message
  • The protection of traffic flow from analysis
    • This requires that an attacker not be able to observe the source and destination, frequency, length, or other characteristics of the traffic on a communications facility

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Confidentiality is the protection of transmitted data from passive attacks. With respect to the content of a data transmission, several levels of protection can be identified. The broadest service protects all user data transmitted between two users over a period of time. For example, when a TCP connection is set up between two systems, this broad protection prevents the release of any user data transmitted over the TCP connection. Narrower forms of this service can also be defined, including the protection of a single message or even specific fields within a message. These refinements are less useful than the broad approach and may even be more complex and expensive to implement. The other aspect of confidentiality is the protection of traffic flow from analysis. This requires that an attacker not be able to observe the source and destination, frequency, length, or other characteristics of the traffic on a communications facility.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. The protection of transmitted data from passive attacks

    سرية البيانات: حماية البيانات المنقولة من الهجمات السلبية.

    Data confidentiality: protecting transmitted data from passive attacks.

  2. Broadest service protects all user data transmitted between two users over a period of time

    أوسع شكل: حماية كل البيانات بين مستخدمين خلال فترة زمنية.

    Broadest form: protects all user data between two users over a period of time.

  3. Narrower forms of service includes the protection of a single message or even specific fields within a message

    أشكال أضيق: حماية رسالة واحدة أو حقول معينة داخلها.

    Narrower forms: protect a single message or specific fields within it.

  4. The protection of traffic flow from analysis

    وتشمل أيضًا حماية تدفق المرور من التحليل.

    It also covers protecting traffic flow from analysis.

  5. This requires that an attacker not be able to observe the source and destination, frequency, length, or other characteristics of the traffic on a communications facility

    أي ألا يرى المهاجم المصدر والوجهة والتكرار والطول وخصائص المرور الأخرى.

    The attacker must not be able to observe source, destination, frequency, length or other traffic characteristics.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

هذه الخدمة تواجه نوعي الهجوم السلبي من الشريحة 13: كشف المحتوى (بحماية البيانات) وتحليل المرور (بحماية تدفق المرور).

This service counters both passive attacks from slide 13: release of contents (by protecting data) and traffic analysis (by protecting traffic flow).

الخلاصة

سرية البيانات = حماية المحتوى + حماية تدفق المرور من التحليل.
Data confidentiality = protecting content + protecting traffic flow from analysis.

الشريحة 20 — Data Integrity

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Can apply to a stream of messages, a single message, or selected fields within a message
  • Connection-oriented integrity service, one that deals with a stream of messages, assures that messages are received as sent with no duplication, insertion, modification, reordering, or replays
  • A connectionless integrity service, one that deals with individual messages without regard to any larger context, generally provides protection against message modification only

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

As with confidentiality, integrity can apply to a stream of messages, a single message, or selected fields within a message. Again, the most useful and straightforward approach is total stream protection. A connection-oriented integrity service, one that deals with a stream of messages, assures that messages are received as sent with no duplication, insertion, modification, reordering, or replays. The destruction of data is also covered under this service. Thus, the connection-oriented integrity service addresses both message stream modification and denial of service. On the other hand, a connectionless integrity service, one that deals with individual messages without regard to any larger context, generally provides protection against message modification only. We can make a distinction between service with and without recovery. Because the integrity service relates to active attacks, we are concerned with detection rather than prevention. If a violation of integrity is detected, then the service may simply report this violation, and some other portion of software or human intervention is required to recover from the violation. Alternatively, there are mechanisms available to recover from the loss of integrity of data, as we will review subsequently. The incorporation of automated recovery mechanisms is, in general, the more attractive alternative.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Can apply to a stream of messages, a single message, or selected fields within a message

    تُطبق على تدفق رسائل، أو رسالة واحدة، أو حقول مختارة.

    Applies to a stream of messages, a single message, or selected fields.

  2. Connection-oriented integrity service … assures that messages are received as sent with no duplication, insertion, modification, reordering, or replays

    النوع الموجّه بالاتصال: يضمن وصول الرسائل كما أُرسلت، بلا تكرار أو إدراج أو تعديل أو إعادة ترتيب أو إعادة إرسال.

    Connection-oriented: messages arrive as sent, with no duplication, insertion, modification, reordering or replay.

  3. A connectionless integrity service … generally provides protection against message modification only

    النوع عديم الاتصال: يتعامل مع كل رسالة منفردة، ويحمي من التعديل فقط.

    Connectionless: handles each message alone and protects against modification only.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

لماذا الفرق؟ لأن الخدمة الموجّهة بالاتصال ترى «السياق» (الترتيب، العدد)، فتكتشف التكرار وإعادة الترتيب. أما عديمة الاتصال فترى كل رسالة وحدها، فلا تعرف إن كانت مكررة.

Why the difference? A connection-oriented service sees context (order, count), so it detects duplication and reordering. A connectionless one sees each message alone, so it can't tell a duplicate.

الخلاصة

موجّهة بالاتصال: تحمي من 5 أشياء؛ عديمة الاتصال: من التعديل فقط.
Connection-oriented: protects against five things; connectionless: modification only.

الشريحة 21 — Nonrepudiation

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Prevents either sender or receiver from denying a transmitted message
  • When a message is sent, the receiver can prove that the alleged sender in fact sent the message
  • When a message is received, the sender can prove that the alleged receiver in fact received the message

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Nonrepudiation prevents either sender or receiver from denying a transmitted message. Thus, when a message is sent, the receiver can prove that the alleged sender in fact sent the message. Similarly, when a message is received, the sender can prove that the alleged receiver in fact received the message.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Prevents either sender or receiver from denying a transmitted message

    عدم الإنكار: يمنع المرسل أو المستلم من إنكار رسالة.

    Nonrepudiation stops sender or receiver from denying a message.

  2. When a message is sent, the receiver can prove that the alleged sender in fact sent the message

    المستلم يستطيع إثبات أن المرسل أرسلها فعلًا.

    The receiver can prove the sender really sent it.

  3. When a message is received, the sender can prove that the alleged receiver in fact received the message

    المرسل يستطيع إثبات أن المستلم استلمها فعلًا.

    The sender can prove the receiver really received it.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

مثال: عميل يرسل أمر شراء أسهم ثم ينخفض السعر فيقول «لم أرسله». عدم الإنكار (عادة بالتوقيع الرقمي) يثبت أنه أرسله. الصورة (أيقونة شخص وظرف بريد) زخرفية.

Example: a client sends a share-purchase order, the price drops, and they claim “I never sent it”. Nonrepudiation (usually via digital signature) proves they did. The image (a person icon and an envelope) is decorative.

الخلاصة

عدم الإنكار: إثبات في الاتجاهين، الإرسال والاستلام.
Nonrepudiation: proof in both directions, sending and receiving.

الشريحة 22 — Availability Service

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Protects a system to ensure its availability
  • This service addresses the security concerns raised by denial-of-service attacks
  • It depends on proper management and control of system resources and thus depends on access control service and other security services

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Availability is the property of a system or a system resource being accessible and usable upon demand by an authorized system entity, according to performance specifications for the system (i.e., a system is available if it provides services according to the system design whenever users request them). A variety of attacks can result in the loss of or reduction in availability. Some of these attacks are amenable to automated countermeasures, such as authentication and encryption, whereas others require some sort of physical action to prevent or recover from loss of availability of elements of a distributed system. X.800 treats availability as a property to be associated with various security services. However, it makes sense to call out specifically an availability service. An availability service is one that protects a system to ensure its availability. This service addresses the security concerns raised by denial-of-service attacks. It depends on proper management and control of system resources and thus depends on access control service and other security services.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Protects a system to ensure its availability

    تحمي النظام لضمان إتاحته.

    Protects a system to ensure it is available.

  2. This service addresses the security concerns raised by denial-of-service attacks

    تواجه هجمات حجب الخدمة.

    Addresses denial-of-service attacks.

  3. It depends on proper management and control of system resources and thus depends on access control service and other security services

    تعتمد على إدارة الموارد، وبالتالي على خدمة التحكم في الوصول وخدمات أخرى.

    Depends on managing resources, and so on access control and other services.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

الآن اكتملت الخدمات الست من الشكل 1.2: المصادقة (16–17)، التحكم في الوصول (18)، سرية البيانات (19)، سلامة البيانات (20)، عدم الإنكار (21)، الإتاحة (22).

All six services from Figure 1.2 are now covered: authentication (16–17), access control (18), data confidentiality (19), data integrity (20), nonrepudiation (21), availability (22).

الخلاصة

خدمة الإتاحة تواجه حجب الخدمة وتعتمد على خدمات أخرى.
The availability service counters DoS and depends on other services.

الشريحة 23 — Security Mechanisms

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Cryptographic algorithms: We can distinguish between reversible cryptographic mechanisms and irreversible cryptographic mechanisms. A reversible cryptographic mechanism is simply an encryption algorithm that allows data to be encrypted and subsequently decrypted. Irreversible cryptographic mechanisms include hash algorithms and message authentication codes, which are used in digital signature and message authentication applications.
  • Data integrity: This category covers a variety of mechanisms used to assure the integrity of a data unit or stream of data units.
  • Digital signature: Data appended to, or a cryptographic transformation of, a data unit that allows a recipient of the data unit to prove the source and integrity of the data unit and protect against forgery.
  • Authentication exchange: A mechanism intended to ensure the identity of an entity by means of information exchange.
  • Traffic padding: The insertion of bits into gaps in a data stream to frustrate traffic analysis attempts.
  • Routing control: Enables selection of particular physically or logically secure routes for certain data and allows routing changes, especially when a breach of security is suspected.
  • Notarization: The use of a trusted third party to assure certain properties of a data exchange
  • Access control: A variety of mechanisms that enforce access rights to resources.

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Figure 1.2c lists the most important security mechanism discussed in this book. These mechanisms will be covered in the appropriate places in the book. So, we do not elaborate now, except to provide the following brief definitions. ■ Cryptographic algorithms: We can distinguish between reversible cryptographic mechanisms and irreversible cryptographic mechanisms. A reversible cryptographic mechanism is simply an encryption algorithm that allows data to be encrypted and subsequently decrypted. Irreversible cryptographic mechanisms include hash algorithms and message authentication codes, which are used in digital signature and message authentication applications. ■ Data integrity: This category covers a variety of mechanisms used to assure the integrity of a data unit or stream of data units. ■ Digital signature: Data appended to, or a cryptographic transformation of, a data unit that allows a recipient of the data unit to prove the source and integrity of the data unit and protect against forgery. ■ Authentication exchange: A mechanism intended to ensure the identity of an entity by means of information exchange. ■ Traffic padding: The insertion of bits into gaps in a data stream to frustrate traffic analysis attempts. ■ Routing control: Enables selection of particular physically or logically secure routes for certain data and allows routing changes, especially when a breach of security is suspected. ■ Notarization: The use of a trusted third party to assure certain properties of a data exchange ■  Access control: A variety of mechanisms that enforce access rights to resources.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Cryptographic algorithms: … reversible cryptographic mechanisms and irreversible cryptographic mechanisms.

    خوارزميات التشفير: نوعان؛ قابلة للعكس (تشفير ثم فك تشفير) وغير قابلة للعكس (دوال التجزئة ورموز مصادقة الرسائل MAC، وتُستخدم في التوقيع الرقمي ومصادقة الرسائل).

    Cryptographic algorithms: reversible (encrypt then decrypt) and irreversible (hash functions and MACs, used for digital signatures and message authentication).

  2. Data integrity: … mechanisms used to assure the integrity of a data unit or stream of data units.

    آليات سلامة البيانات لوحدة بيانات أو تدفق منها.

    Mechanisms ensuring the integrity of a data unit or stream.

  3. Digital signature: Data appended to, or a cryptographic transformation of, a data unit that allows a recipient … to prove the source and integrity of the data unit and protect against forgery.

    التوقيع الرقمي: بيانات تُضاف للرسالة (أو تحويل تشفيري لها) تثبت المصدر والسلامة وتحمي من التزوير.

    Digital signature: data appended to (or a transformation of) a data unit proving source and integrity and preventing forgery.

  4. Authentication exchange: A mechanism intended to ensure the identity of an entity by means of information exchange.

    تبادل المصادقة: التحقق من الهوية بتبادل معلومات (مثل كلمة مرور أو تحدٍّ واستجابة).

    Authentication exchange: verifying identity by exchanging information (e.g. password, challenge-response).

  5. Traffic padding: The insertion of bits into gaps in a data stream to frustrate traffic analysis attempts.

    حشو المرور: إدخال بتات في فجوات التدفق لإفشال تحليل المرور.

    Traffic padding: inserting bits into gaps to defeat traffic analysis.

  6. Routing control: Enables selection of particular physically or logically secure routes … especially when a breach of security is suspected.

    التحكم في التوجيه: اختيار مسارات آمنة، وتغييرها عند الاشتباه بخرق.

    Routing control: choosing secure routes and changing them when a breach is suspected.

  7. Notarization: The use of a trusted third party to assure certain properties of a data exchange

    التوثيق: طرف ثالث موثوق يضمن خصائص معينة لتبادل البيانات.

    Notarization: a trusted third party vouches for properties of a data exchange.

  8. Access control: A variety of mechanisms that enforce access rights to resources.

    التحكم في الوصول: آليات تفرض صلاحيات الوصول.

    Access control: mechanisms enforcing access rights.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

اربط كل آلية بالخدمة أو الهجوم: حشو المرور ← تحليل المرور؛ التوقيع الرقمي ← عدم الإنكار والسلامة؛ تبادل المصادقة ← المصادقة؛ التوثيق ← عدم الإنكار؛ التحكم في التوجيه ← السرية عند الاشتباه.

Link each mechanism to a service or attack: traffic padding → traffic analysis; digital signature → nonrepudiation and integrity; authentication exchange → authentication; notarization → nonrepudiation; routing control → confidentiality when a breach is suspected.

الخلاصة

8 آليات؛ التشفير منها قابل للعكس وغير قابل للعكس.
8 mechanisms; cryptographic ones are reversible or irreversible.
