📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Cryptographic algorithms can be divided into three categories (Figure 1.4): Keyless: Do not use any keys during cryptographic transformations. Single-key: The result of a transformation are a function of the input data and a single key, known as a secret key. Two-key: At various stages of the calculation, two different but related keys are used, referred to as private key and public key.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Keyless / Single-Key / Two-Key

    تصنيف الخوارزميات حسب عدد المفاتيح: صفر، واحد، اثنان.

    Algorithms classified by number of keys: zero, one, two.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

الشرائح 25–28 تشرح كل عمود. لاحظ أن الـ MAC يقع تحت «مفتاح واحد» لأنه يحتاج مفتاحًا سريًا، رغم أنه يستخدم دالة تجزئة.

Slides 25–28 explain each column. Note that MAC sits under single-key because it needs a secret key, even though it uses a hash function.

الخلاصة

بلا مفتاح: تجزئة وPRNG؛ مفتاح واحد: كتلة، تدفق، MAC؛ مفتاحان: تشفير غير متماثل، توقيع، تبادل مفاتيح، مصادقة مستخدم.
Keyless: hash, PRNG; single-key: block, stream, MAC; two-key: asymmetric encryption, signature, key exchange, user authentication.

الشريحة 25 — Keyless Algorithms

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Deterministic functions that have certain properties useful for cryptography
  • One type of keyless algorithm is the cryptographic hash function
    • A hash function turns a variable amount of text into a small, fixed-length value called a hash value, hash code, or digest
      • A cryptographic hash function is one that has additional properties that make it useful as part of another cryptographic algorithm, such as a message authentication code or a digital signature
      • A pseudorandom number generator produces a deterministic sequence of numbers or bits that has the appearance of being a truly random sequence

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Keyless algorithms are deterministic functions that have certain properties useful for cryptography. One important type of keyless algorithm is the cryptographic hash function. A hash function turns a variable amount of text into a small, fixed-length value called a hash value, hash code, or digest. A cryptographic hash function is one that has additional properties that make it useful as part of another cryptographic algorithm, such as a message authentication code or a digital signature. A pseudorandom number generator produces a deterministic sequence of numbers or bits that has the appearance of being a truly random sequence. Although the sequence appears to lack any definite pattern, it will repeat after a certain sequence length. Nevertheless, for some cryptographic purposes this apparently random sequence is sufficient.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Deterministic functions that have certain properties useful for cryptography

    دوال حتمية (نفس المدخل يعطي نفس المخرج دائمًا) لها خصائص مفيدة للتشفير.

    Deterministic functions (same input → same output) with properties useful for cryptography.

  2. One type of keyless algorithm is the cryptographic hash function

    مثال: دالة التجزئة التشفيرية.

    One example: the cryptographic hash function.

  3. A hash function turns a variable amount of text into a small, fixed-length value called a hash value, hash code, or digest

    دالة التجزئة تحول نصًا بأي طول إلى قيمة صغيرة ثابتة الطول تسمى hash value أو hash code أو digest.

    A hash function maps text of any length to a small fixed-length value: hash value, hash code, or digest.

  4. A cryptographic hash function is one that has additional properties that make it useful as part of another cryptographic algorithm, such as a message authentication code or a digital signature

    التجزئة «التشفيرية» لها خصائص إضافية تجعلها مفيدة داخل خوارزميات أخرى كـ MAC والتوقيع الرقمي.

    A cryptographic hash has extra properties making it useful inside MACs and digital signatures.

  5. A pseudorandom number generator produces a deterministic sequence of numbers or bits that has the appearance of being a truly random sequence

    مولد الأرقام شبه العشوائية: ينتج تسلسلًا حتميًا يبدو عشوائيًا تمامًا.

    A PRNG produces a deterministic sequence that looks truly random.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

«شبه» عشوائي لأنه حتمي: إذا عرفت نقطة البداية (البذرة) تستطيع إعادة إنتاج نفس التسلسل. لكنه يبدو عشوائيًا لمن لا يعرفها.

“Pseudo”-random because it is deterministic: knowing the starting point (seed) reproduces the same sequence. It just looks random to anyone who doesn't.

الخلاصة

خوارزميات بلا مفتاح: دوال تجزئة تشفيرية ومولدات أرقام شبه عشوائية.
Keyless algorithms: cryptographic hash functions and pseudorandom number generators.

الشريحة 26 — Single-Key Algorithms

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Single-key cryptographic algorithms depend on the use of a secret key
  • Encryption algorithms that use a single key are referred to as symmetric encryption algorithms
  • With symmetric encryption, an encryption algorithm takes as input some data to be protected and a secret key and produces an unintelligible transformation on that data
  • A corresponding decryption algorithm takes the transformed data and the same secret key and recovers the original data
  • Symmetric encryption takes the following forms:
  • Block cipher
    • A block cipher operates on data as a sequence of blocks
    • In most versions of the block cipher, known as modes of operation, the transformation depends not only on the current data block and the secret key but also on the content of preceding blocks
  • Stream cipher
    • A stream cipher operates on data as a sequence of bits
    • As with the block cipher, the transformation depends on a secret key

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Single-key cryptographic algorithms depend on the use of a secret key. This key may be known to a single user; for example, this is the case for protecting stored data that is only going to be accessed by the data creator. Commonly, two parties share the secret key so that communication between the two parties is protected. For certain applications, more than two users may share the same secret key. In this last case, the algorithm protects data from those outside the group who share the key. Encryption algorithms that use a single key are referred to as symmetric encryption algorithms. With symmetric encryption, an encryption algorithm takes as input some data to be protected and a secret key and produces an unintelligible transformation on that data. A corresponding decryption algorithm takes the transformed data and the same secret key and recovers the original data. Symmetric encryption takes the following forms: ■ Block cipher: A block cipher operates on data as a sequence of blocks. A typical block size is 128 bits. In most versions of the block cipher, known as modes of operation, the transformation depends not only on the current data block and the secret key but also on the content of preceding blocks. ■ Stream cipher: A stream cipher operates on data as a sequence of bits. Typically, an exclusive-OR operation is used to produce a bit-by-bit transformation. As with the block cipher, the transformation depends on a secret key.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Single-key cryptographic algorithms depend on the use of a secret key

    خوارزميات المفتاح الواحد تعتمد على مفتاح سري.

    Single-key algorithms rely on a secret key.

  2. Encryption algorithms that use a single key are referred to as symmetric encryption algorithms

    تسمى خوارزميات التشفير المتماثل.

    They are called symmetric encryption algorithms.

  3. With symmetric encryption, an encryption algorithm takes as input some data to be protected and a secret key and produces an unintelligible transformation on that data

    التشفير يأخذ البيانات والمفتاح وينتج شكلًا غير مفهوم.

    Encryption takes data plus key and produces an unintelligible form.

  4. A corresponding decryption algorithm takes the transformed data and the same secret key and recovers the original data

    فك التشفير يأخذ الناتج ونفس المفتاح ويستعيد البيانات.

    Decryption takes that output plus the same key and recovers the data.

  5. Block cipher — operates on data as a sequence of blocks … the transformation depends not only on the current data block and the secret key but also on the content of preceding blocks

    شيفرة الكتلة: تعمل على كتل؛ وفي معظم «أنماط التشغيل» يعتمد التحويل على الكتلة الحالية والمفتاح والكتل السابقة.

    Block cipher: works on blocks; in most modes of operation the output depends on the current block, the key and earlier blocks.

  6. Stream cipher — operates on data as a sequence of bits … the transformation depends on a secret key

    شيفرة التدفق: تعمل على البيانات بتًا بتًا، وتعتمد على مفتاح سري.

    Stream cipher: works bit by bit and depends on a secret key.

الشريحة 27 — Single-Key Algorithms — Message Authentication Code

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Another form of single-key cryptographic algorithm is the message authentication code (MAC)
  • A MAC is a data element associated with a data block or message
  • The MAC is generated by a cryptographic transformation involving a secret key and, typically, a cryptographic hash function of the message
  • The MAC is designed so that someone in possession of the secret key can verify the integrity of the message
  • The recipient of the message plus the MAC can perform the same calculation on the message; if the calculated MAC matches the MAC accompanying the message, this provides assurance that the message has not been altered

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Another form of single-key cryptographic algorithm is the message authentication code (MAC). A MAC is a data element associated with a data block or message. The MAC is generated by a cryptographic transformation involving a secret key and, typically, a cryptographic hash function of the message. The MAC is designed so that someone in possession of the secret key can verify the integrity of the message. Thus, the MAC algorithm takes as input a message and secret key and produces the MAC. The recipient of the message plus the MAC can perform the same calculation on the message; if the calculated MAC matches the MAC accompanying the message, this provides assurance that the message has not been altered.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Another form of single-key cryptographic algorithm is the message authentication code (MAC)

    نوع آخر بمفتاح واحد: رمز مصادقة الرسالة MAC.

    Another single-key form: the message authentication code (MAC).

  2. A MAC is a data element associated with a data block or message

    MAC عنصر بيانات مرتبط برسالة.

    A MAC is a data element attached to a message.

  3. The MAC is generated by a cryptographic transformation involving a secret key and, typically, a cryptographic hash function of the message

    يُحسب من المفتاح السري وعادة من دالة تجزئة للرسالة.

    Computed from the secret key and usually a cryptographic hash of the message.

  4. The MAC is designed so that someone in possession of the secret key can verify the integrity of the message

    من يملك المفتاح يستطيع التحقق من سلامة الرسالة.

    Anyone with the key can verify the message's integrity.

  5. The recipient … can perform the same calculation on the message; if the calculated MAC matches the MAC accompanying the message, this provides assurance that the message has not been altered

    المستلم يعيد الحساب؛ إذا تطابقت النتيجة مع الـ MAC المرفق فالرسالة لم تتغير.

    The recipient recomputes it; if it matches the attached MAC, the message was not altered.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

Sender:   MAC = F(K, message)  -> send (message, MAC)
Receiver: MAC' = F(K, message received)
          MAC' == MAC ?  yes -> not altered   no -> altered

المهاجم الذي يغيّر الرسالة لا يستطيع حساب MAC صحيح جديد لأنه لا يملك K.

Sender:   MAC = F(K, message)  -> send (message, MAC)
Receiver: MAC' = F(K, message received)
          MAC' == MAC ?  yes -> not altered   no -> altered

An attacker who changes the message can't compute a valid new MAC without K.

الخلاصة

MAC = قيمة من المفتاح والرسالة؛ تطابقها يثبت عدم التعديل.
MAC = a value from key and message; a match proves no alteration.

الشريحة 28 — Asymmetric Algorithms

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Encryption algorithms that use a single key are referred to as asymmetric encryption algorithms
  • Digital signature algorithm
    • A digital signature is a value computed with a cryptographic algorithm and associated with a data object in such a way that any recipient of the data can use the signature to verify the data’s origin and integrity
  • Key exchange
    • The process of securely distributing a symmetric key to two or more parties
  • User authentication
    • The process of authenticating that a user attempting to access an application or service is genuine and, similarly, that the application or service is genuine

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

[Note: the first bullet on the slide says “a single key”; per Figure 1.4 and the textbook, asymmetric algorithms use two keys. The source wording is kept as is.]

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Two-key algorithms involve the use of two related keys. A private key is known only to a single user or entity, whereas the corresponding public key is made available to a number of users. Encryption algorithms that use a single key are referred to as asymmetric encryption algorithms. Asymmetric encryption can work in two ways: An encryption algorithm takes as input some data to be protected and the private key and produces an unintelligible transformation on that data. A corresponding decryption algorithm takes the transformed data and the corresponding public key and recovers the original data. In this case, only the possessor of the private key can have performed the encryption and any possessor of the public key can perform the decryption. An encryption algorithm takes as input some data to be protected and a public key and produces an unintelligible transformation on that data. A corresponding decryption algorithm takes the transformed data and the corresponding private key and recovers the original data. In this case, any possessor of the public key can have performed the encryption and only the possessor of the private key can perform the decryption. Asymmetric encryption has a variety of applications. One of the most important is the digital signature algorithm. A digital signature is a value computed with a cryptographic algorithm and associated with a data object in such a way that any recipient of the data can use the signature to verify the data’s origin and integrity. Typically, the signer of a data object uses the signer’s private key to generate the signature, and anyone in possession of the corresponding public key can verify that validity of the signature. Asymmetric algorithms can also be used in two other important applications. Key exchange is the process of securely distributing a symmetric key to two or more parties. User authentication is the process of authenticating that a user attempting to access an application or service is genuine and, similarly, that the application or service is genuine. These concepts are explained in detail in subsequent chapters.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Encryption algorithms that use a single key are referred to as asymmetric encryption algorithms

    الشريحة تقول «مفتاح واحد» وهذا خطأ في الشريحة: الخوارزميات غير المتماثلة تستخدم مفتاحين (عام وخاص)، كما في عمود Two-Key بالشكل 1.4.

    The slide says “a single key”, which is a slide error: asymmetric algorithms use two keys (public and private), as in the Two-Key column of Figure 1.4.

  2. Digital signature algorithm — … any recipient of the data can use the signature to verify the data’s origin and integrity

    التوقيع الرقمي: قيمة مرتبطة بالبيانات تسمح لأي مستلم بالتحقق من مصدرها وسلامتها.

    Digital signature: a value tied to the data that lets any recipient verify origin and integrity.

  3. Key exchange — The process of securely distributing a symmetric key to two or more parties

    تبادل المفاتيح: توزيع مفتاح متماثل بأمان على طرفين أو أكثر.

    Key exchange: securely distributing a symmetric key to two or more parties.

  4. User authentication — … a user attempting to access an application or service is genuine and, similarly, that the application or service is genuine

    مصادقة المستخدم: التأكد أن المستخدم حقيقي، وأن الخدمة نفسها حقيقية.

    User authentication: confirming the user is genuine, and that the service is too.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

لاحظ الفرق مع MAC: MAC يتحقق منه فقط من يملك المفتاح السري، أما التوقيع الرقمي فيتحقق منه أي مستلم. وتبادل المفاتيح غير المتماثل يحل مشكلة توزيع المفتاح المتماثل.

Contrast with MAC: only key holders can verify a MAC, but any recipient can verify a digital signature. Asymmetric key exchange solves the problem of distributing symmetric keys.

الخلاصة

غير متماثل (مفتاحان): تشفير، توقيع رقمي، تبادل مفاتيح، مصادقة مستخدم.
Asymmetric (two keys): encryption, digital signature, key exchange, user authentication.

الشريحة 30 — Communications Security

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Deals with the protection of communications through the network, including measures to protect against both passive and active attacks
  • Communications security is primarily implemented using network protocols
    • A network protocol consists of the format and procedures that governs the transmitting and receiving of data between points in a network
      • A protocol defines the structure of the individual data units and the control commands that manage the data transfer
  • With respect to network security, a security protocol may be an enhancement that is part of an existing protocol or a standalone protocol

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

In the context of network security, communications security deals with the protection of communications through the network, including measures to protect against both passive and active attacks (Figure 1.3). Communications security is primarily implemented using network protocols. A network protocol consists of the format and procedures that governs the transmitting and receiving of data between points in a network. A protocol defines the structure of the individual data units (e.g., packets) and the control commands that manage the data transfer. With respect to network security, a security protocol may be an enhancement that is part of an existing protocol or a standalone protocol. Examples of the former are IPsec, which is part of the Internet Protocol (IP) and IEEE 802.11i, which is part of the IEEE 802.11 Wi-Fi standard. Examples of the latter are Transport Layer Security (TLS) and Secure Shell (SSH). Part Six examines these and other secure network protocols. One common characteristic of all of these protocols is that they use a number of cryptographic algorithms as part of the mechanism to provide security.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Deals with the protection of communications through the network, including measures to protect against both passive and active attacks

    حماية الاتصالات عبر الشبكة ضد الهجمات السلبية والنشطة.

    Protecting communications over the network against passive and active attacks.

  2. Communications security is primarily implemented using network protocols

    تُنفذ أساسًا بالبروتوكولات.

    Implemented mainly through network protocols.

  3. A network protocol consists of the format and procedures that governs the transmitting and receiving of data between points in a network

    البروتوكول: الصيغة والإجراءات التي تحكم الإرسال والاستقبال.

    A protocol is the format and procedures governing sending and receiving.

  4. A protocol defines the structure of the individual data units and the control commands that manage the data transfer

    يحدد بنية وحدات البيانات وأوامر التحكم.

    It defines data-unit structure and control commands.

  5. With respect to network security, a security protocol may be an enhancement that is part of an existing protocol or a standalone protocol

    البروتوكول الأمني قد يكون إضافة لبروتوكول موجود أو بروتوكولًا مستقلًا.

    A security protocol may extend an existing protocol or stand alone.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

مثال (إضافي): HTTPS هو HTTP مع طبقة TLS، أي إضافة أمنية لبروتوكول موجود، بينما SSH بروتوكول أمني مستقل.

Example (additional): HTTPS is HTTP plus TLS, a security add-on to an existing protocol, while SSH is a standalone security protocol.

الخلاصة

أمن الاتصالات يُبنى بالبروتوكولات الأمنية (إضافية أو مستقلة).
Communications security is built with security protocols (add-on or standalone).

الشريحة 31 — Device Security

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • The other aspect of network security is the protection of network devices, such as routers and switches, and end systems connected to the network, such as client systems and servers
  • The primary security concerns are intruders that gain access to the system to perform unauthorized actions, insert malicious software (malware), or overwhelm system resources to diminish availability
  • Three types of device security are:
    • Firewall
      • A hardware and/or software capability that limits access between a network and device attached to the network, in accordance with a specific security policy. The firewall acts as a filter that permits or denies data traffic, both incoming and outgoing, based on a set of rules based on traffic content and/or traffic pattern
      • Intrusion detection
        • Hardware or software products that gather and analyze information from various areas within a computer or a network for the purpose of finding, and providing real-time or near-real-time warning of, attempts to access system resources in an unauthorized manner
      • Intrusion prevention
        • Hardware or software products designed to detect intrusive activity and attempt to stop the activity, ideally before it reaches its target

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

The other aspect of network security is the protection of network devices, such as routers and switches, and end systems connected to the network, such as client systems and servers. The primary security concerns are intruders that gain access to the system to perform unauthorized actions, insert malicious software (malware), or overwhelm system resources to diminish availability. Three types of device security are noteworthy: ■ Firewall: A hardware and/or software capability that limits access between a network and device attached to the network, in accordance with a specific security policy. The firewall acts as a filter that permits or denies data traffic, both incoming and outgoing, based on a set of rules based on traffic content and/or traffic pattern. ■ Intrusion detection: Hardware or software products that gather and analyze information from various areas within a computer or a network for the purpose of finding, and providing real-time or near-real-time warning of, attempts to access system resources in an unauthorized manner. ■ Intrusion prevention: Hardware or software products designed to detect intrusive activity and attempt to stop the activity, ideally before it reaches its target. These device security capabilities are more closely related to the field of computer security than network security. Accordingly, they are dealt with more briefly than communications security in Part Six. For a more detailed treatment, see [STAL18].

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. The other aspect of network security is the protection of network devices, such as routers and switches, and end systems connected to the network, such as client systems and servers

    الوجه الآخر: حماية أجهزة الشبكة (موجهات، محولات) والأنظمة الطرفية (عملاء، خوادم).

    The other side: protecting network devices (routers, switches) and end systems (clients, servers).

  2. The primary security concerns are intruders that gain access to the system to perform unauthorized actions, insert malicious software (malware), or overwhelm system resources to diminish availability

    المخاوف: متسللون ينفذون أفعالًا غير مصرح بها، أو يزرعون برامج خبيثة، أو يستنزفون الموارد فيقللون الإتاحة.

    Concerns: intruders doing unauthorized actions, planting malware, or exhausting resources to reduce availability.

  3. Firewall — … acts as a filter that permits or denies data traffic, both incoming and outgoing, based on a set of rules

    الجدار الناري: مرشح يسمح أو يمنع المرور الداخل والخارج حسب قواعد وسياسة أمنية.

    Firewall: a filter allowing or denying inbound and outbound traffic by rules and policy.

  4. Intrusion detection — … finding, and providing real-time or near-real-time warning of, attempts to access system resources in an unauthorized manner

    كشف التسلل: يجمع المعلومات ويحللها ويُطلق تحذيرًا فوريًا أو شبه فوري عند محاولات الوصول غير المصرح.

    Intrusion detection: gathers and analyses information and warns in (near) real time of unauthorized access attempts.

  5. Intrusion prevention — … detect intrusive activity and attempt to stop the activity, ideally before it reaches its target

    منع التسلل: يكشف النشاط ويحاول إيقافه، ويفضّل قبل وصوله لهدفه.

    Intrusion prevention: detects intrusive activity and tries to stop it, ideally before it reaches its target.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

الفرق بين الاثنين الأخيرين: كشف التسلل (IDS) يُنبّه فقط، ومنع التسلل (IPS) يتدخل ويوقف.

The difference: intrusion detection (IDS) only alerts; intrusion prevention (IPS) intervenes and stops.

الخلاصة

أمن الأجهزة: جدار ناري (يرشح)، كشف تسلل (ينبه)، منع تسلل (يوقف).
Device security: firewall (filters), IDS (alerts), IPS (stops).

الشريحة 32 — Trust Model

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • One of the most widely accepted and most cited definitions of trust is:
    • “the willingness of a party to be vulnerable to the actions of
      • another party based on the expectation that the other will perform
      • a particular action important to the trustor, irrespective of the ability
      • to monitor or control that other party”
  • Three related concepts are relevant to a trust model:
    • Trustworthiness: A characteristic of an entity that reflects the degree to which that entity is deserving of trust
      • Propensity to trust: A tendency to be willing to trust others across a broad spectrum of situations and trust targets. This suggests that every individual has some baseline level of trust that will influence the person’s willingness to rely on the words and actions of others
      • Risk: A measure of the extent to which an entity is threatened by a potential circumstance or event, and typically a function of 1) the adverse impacts that would arise if the circumstance or event occurs; and 2) the likelihood of occurrence

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

One of the most widely accepted and most cited definitions of trust in the organizational science literature is from [MAYE95], which defines trust as follows: the willingness of a party to be vulnerable to the actions of another party based on the expectation that the other will perform a particular action important to the trustor, irrespective of the ability to monitor or control that other party. Three related concepts are relevant to a trust model: ■ Trustworthiness: A characteristic of an entity that reflects the degree to which that entity is deserving of trust. ■ Propensity to trust: A tendency to be willing to trust others across a broad spectrum of situations and trust targets. This suggests that every individual has some baseline level of trust that will influence the person’s willingness to rely on the words and actions of others. ■ Risk: A measure of the extent to which an entity is threatened by a potential circumstance or event, and typically a function of 1) the adverse impacts that would arise if the circumstance or event occurs; and 2) the likelihood of occurrence.

الصيغ

Risk = f(impact, likelihood)

قراءة قارئ الشاشة: الخطر دالة في الأثر والاحتمال.Risk is a function of impact and likelihood.

كتابة مختصرة للتعريف النصي في الشريحة، وليست صيغة مكتوبة فيها.

A shorthand for the slide's verbal definition, not a formula printed on it.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. “the willingness of a party to be vulnerable to the actions of another party based on the expectation that the other will perform a particular action important to the trustor, irrespective of the ability to monitor or control that other party”

    تعريف الثقة: استعداد طرف لأن يكون معرضًا لأفعال طرف آخر، متوقعًا أنه سيؤدي فعلًا مهمًا له، حتى بدون قدرة على مراقبته أو التحكم فيه.

    Trust: a party's willingness to be vulnerable to another's actions, expecting them to perform an important action, without being able to monitor or control them.

  2. Trustworthiness: A characteristic of an entity that reflects the degree to which that entity is deserving of trust

    الجدارة بالثقة: صفة في الكيان تعكس مدى استحقاقه للثقة.

    Trustworthiness: how far an entity deserves trust.

  3. Propensity to trust: A tendency to be willing to trust others across a broad spectrum of situations and trust targets…

    الميل للثقة: نزعة عامة لدى الشخص للثقة بالآخرين؛ لكل فرد مستوى أساسي من الثقة يؤثر في اعتماده على الآخرين.

    Propensity to trust: a general tendency to trust others; everyone has a baseline level that affects reliance on others.

  4. Risk: A measure of the extent to which an entity is threatened by a potential circumstance or event, and typically a function of 1) the adverse impacts … and 2) the likelihood of occurrence

    الخطر: مقياس لمدى تهديد كيان بحدث محتمل، وعادة دالة في (1) حجم الضرر و(2) احتمال الحدوث.

    Risk: how much an entity is threatened by a potential event, usually a function of (1) impact and (2) likelihood.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

المفاهيم الثلاثة معًا: الطرف الواثق له ميل للثقة، ويقيّم جدارة الطرف الآخر، ويوازن ذلك مع الخطر. ملاحظات الشريحة تذكر أن الشكل 1.6 في الكتاب يوضح هذه العلاقة.

Together: the trustor has a propensity to trust, assesses the other's trustworthiness, and weighs it against the risk. The slide notes say Figure 1.6 in the book shows this relationship.

الخلاصة

نموذج الثقة: الجدارة بالثقة، الميل للثقة، الخطر (الأثر × الاحتمال).
Trust model: trustworthiness, propensity to trust, risk (impact and likelihood).

الشريحة 33 — The Trust Model and Information Security

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Trust is confidence that an entity will perform in a way that will not prejudice the security of the user of the system of which that entity is a part
  • Trust is always restricted to specific functions or ways of behavior and is meaningful only in the context of a security policy
  • Generally, an entity is said to trust a second entity when the first entity assumes that the second entity will behave exactly as the first entity expects
  • In this context, the term entity may refer to a single hardware component or software module, a piece of equipment identified by make and model, a site or location, or an organization

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Trust is confidence that an entity will perform in a way that will not prejudice the security of the user of the system of which that entity is a part. Trust is always restricted to specific functions or ways of behavior and is meaningful only in the context of a security policy. Generally, an entity is said to trust a second entity when the first entity assumes that the second entity will behave exactly as the first entity expects. This trust may apply only for some specific function. In this context, the term entity may refer to a single hardware component or software module, a piece of equipment identified by make and model, a site or location, or an organization.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Trust is confidence that an entity will perform in a way that will not prejudice the security of the user of the system of which that entity is a part

    الثقة: اطمئنان أن الكيان سيتصرف بطريقة لا تضر بأمن المستخدم.

    Trust: confidence an entity will behave without harming the user's security.

  2. Trust is always restricted to specific functions or ways of behavior and is meaningful only in the context of a security policy

    الثقة دائمًا محدودة بوظائف معينة، ولا معنى لها إلا ضمن سياسة أمنية.

    Trust is always limited to specific functions and only makes sense within a security policy.

  3. Generally, an entity is said to trust a second entity when the first entity assumes that the second entity will behave exactly as the first entity expects

    كيان يثق بآخر عندما يفترض أنه سيتصرف كما يتوقع تمامًا.

    An entity trusts another when it assumes the other will behave exactly as expected.

  4. In this context, the term entity may refer to a single hardware component or software module, a piece of equipment identified by make and model, a site or location, or an organization

    «الكيان» قد يكون قطعة عتاد، وحدة برمجية، جهازًا بطرازه، موقعًا، أو منظمة.

    An “entity” may be a hardware component, software module, a device by make and model, a site, or an organization.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

مثال: تثق بمتصفحك في التحقق من شهادات المواقع (وظيفة محددة)، لكن هذا لا يعني أنك تثق به في كل شيء.

Example: you trust your browser to check website certificates (a specific function), which doesn't mean you trust it for everything.

الخلاصة

الثقة في أمن المعلومات محدودة بوظائف وسياسة، والكيان قد يكون أي شيء من مكوّن إلى منظمة.
Trust in information security is limited to functions and a policy; an entity can be anything from a component to an organization.

الشريحة 34 — Trustworthiness of an Individual

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Organizations need to be concerned about both internal users (employees, on-site contractors) and external users (customers, suppliers) of their information systems
  • With respect to internal users, an organization develops a level of trust in individuals by policies in the following two areas:
  • Human resource security
    • Sound security practice dictates that information security requirements be embedded into each stage of the employment life cycle, specifying security-related actions required during the induction of each individual, their ongoing management, and termination of their employment. Human resource security also includes assigning ownership of information (including responsibility for its protection) to capable individuals and obtaining confirmation of their understanding and acceptance
  • Security awareness and training
    • This area refers to disseminating security information to all employees, including IT staff, IT security staff, and management, as well as IT users and other employees. A workforce that has a high level of security awareness and appropriate security training for each individual’s role is as important, if not more important, than any other security countermeasure or control

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Organizations need to be concerned about both internal users (employees, on-site contractors) and external users (customers, suppliers) of their information systems. With respect to internal users, an organization develops a level of trust in individuals by policies in the following two areas [STAL19]: ■ Human resource security: Sound security practice dictates that information security requirements be embedded into each stage of the employment life cycle, specifying security-related actions required during the induction of each individual, their ongoing management, and termination of their employment. Human resource security also includes assigning ownership of information (including responsibility for its protection) to capable individuals and obtaining confirmation of their understanding and acceptance. ■ Security awareness and training: This area refers to disseminating security information to all employees, including IT staff, IT security staff, and management, as well as IT users and other employees. A workforce that has a high level of security awareness and appropriate security training for each individual’s role is as important, if not more important, than any other security countermeasure or control. For external users, trust will depend on the context. In general terms, the factors of perceived trustworthiness and the trustor's propensity, as depicted in Figure 1.6, determine the level of trust. Further, the issue of trust is mutual. That is, not only must an organization determine a level of trust towards external users, but external users need to be concerned about the degree to which they can trust an information resource that they use. This mutual trust involves a number a practical consequences, including the use of a public-key infrastructure and user authentication protocols. These matters are explored in Part Five.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Organizations need to be concerned about both internal users (employees, on-site contractors) and external users (customers, suppliers) of their information systems

    المنظمة تهتم بالمستخدمين الداخليين (موظفون، متعاقدون) والخارجيين (عملاء، موردون).

    Organizations care about internal users (staff, contractors) and external users (customers, suppliers).

  2. With respect to internal users, an organization develops a level of trust in individuals by policies in the following two areas:

    للداخليين: تبني الثقة بسياسات في مجالين.

    For internal users, trust is built through policies in two areas.

  3. Human resource security — … information security requirements be embedded into each stage of the employment life cycle … induction …, ongoing management, and termination of their employment …

    أمن الموارد البشرية: متطلبات الأمن في كل مرحلة وظيفية: التعيين، الإدارة المستمرة، إنهاء الخدمة؛ وإسناد ملكية المعلومات لأشخاص أكفاء مع تأكيد فهمهم.

    HR security: security requirements at every stage of employment: induction, ongoing management, termination; plus assigning information ownership to capable people and confirming their understanding.

  4. Security awareness and training — … A workforce that has a high level of security awareness and appropriate security training … is as important, if not more important, than any other security countermeasure or control

    التوعية والتدريب: نشر المعلومات الأمنية لكل الموظفين؛ وقوة عاملة واعية أمنيًا بنفس أهمية أي إجراء أمني آخر، إن لم تكن أهم.

    Awareness and training: spreading security information to all staff; an aware, trained workforce is as important as, if not more than, any other control.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

الرسالة: التقنية وحدها لا تكفي؛ الموظف غير الواعي قد يفتح رابط تصيد ويُبطل كل الحماية. لهذا يُعدّ العنصر البشري جزءًا من نموذج الثقة.

The message: technology alone isn't enough; an unaware employee can click a phishing link and undo every protection. That is why people are part of the trust model.

الخلاصة

ثقة الأفراد الداخليين تُبنى بأمن الموارد البشرية والتوعية والتدريب.
Trust in internal individuals is built through HR security and awareness/training.

الشريحة 35 — Trustworthiness of an Organization

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Most organizations rely on information system service and information provided by external organizations, as well as partnerships to accomplish missions and business functions (examples are cloud service providers and companies that form part of the supply chain for the organization)
  • To manage risk to the organization, it must establish trust relationships with these external organizations
  • NIST SP 800-39 (Managing Information Security Risk, March 2011) indicates that such trust relationships can be:
    • Formally established, for example, by documenting the trust-related information in contracts, service-level agreements, statements of work, memoranda of agreement/understanding, or interconnection security agreements
      • Scalable and inter-organizational or intra-organizational in nature
      • Represented by simple (bilateral) relationships between two partners or more complex many-to-many relationships among many diverse partners

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Most organizations rely, to a greater or lesser extent, on information system service and information provided by external organizations, as well as partnerships to accomplish missions and business functions. Examples are cloud service providers and companies that form part of the supply chain for the organization. To manage risk to the organization, it must establish trust relationships with these external organizations. NIST SP 800-39 (Managing Information Security Risk, March 2011) indicates that such trust relationships can be: ■ Formally established, for example, by documenting the trust-related information in contracts, service-level agreements, statements of work, memoranda of agreement/understanding, or interconnection security agreements; ■ Scalable and inter-organizational or intra-organizational in nature; and/or ■ Represented by simple (bilateral) relationships between two partners or more complex many-to-many relationships among many diverse partners. The requirements for establishing and maintaining trust depend on mission/business requirements, the participants involved in the trust relationship, the criticality/sensitivity of the information being shared or the types of services being rendered, the history between the organizations, and the overall risk to the organizations participating in the relationship. As with individuals, trust related to organizations can involve the use of public-key infrastructure and user authentication, as well as the network security measures described in Part Six.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Most organizations rely on information system service and information provided by external organizations, as well as partnerships …

    معظم المنظمات تعتمد على خدمات ومعلومات من جهات خارجية (مثل مزودي الحوسبة السحابية وسلسلة التوريد).

    Most organizations rely on external services and information (e.g. cloud providers, supply chain).

  2. To manage risk to the organization, it must establish trust relationships with these external organizations

    لإدارة الخطر يجب بناء علاقات ثقة معها.

    To manage risk, it must build trust relationships with them.

  3. NIST SP 800-39 … indicates that such trust relationships can be: Formally established …

    حسب NIST SP 800-39 (مارس 2011): يمكن أن تكون رسمية (عقود، اتفاقيات مستوى خدمة، مذكرات تفاهم، اتفاقيات ربط أمني).

    Per NIST SP 800-39 (March 2011): they can be formal (contracts, SLAs, MoUs, interconnection security agreements).

  4. Scalable and inter-organizational or intra-organizational in nature

    قابلة للتوسع، وبين المنظمات أو داخلها.

    Scalable, between or within organizations.

  5. Represented by simple (bilateral) relationships between two partners or more complex many-to-many relationships among many diverse partners

    علاقات بسيطة ثنائية أو معقدة متعددة الأطراف.

    Simple bilateral or complex many-to-many relationships.

الشرح — شرح موسّع

مثال: شركة تخزن بياناتها عند مزود سحابي. الثقة به تُوثق في اتفاقية مستوى الخدمة (SLA) التي تحدد التزاماته الأمنية.

Example: a company stores data with a cloud provider; trust is documented in an SLA that sets the provider's security obligations.

الخلاصة

ثقة المنظمات: علاقات مع جهات خارجية، رسمية، قابلة للتوسع، ثنائية أو متعددة.
Organizational trust: relationships with external parties, formal, scalable, bilateral or many-to-many.

الشريحة 36 — Trustworthiness of Information Systems

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • SP 800-39 defines trustworthiness for information systems as
    • “the degree to which information systems (including the information technology products from which the systems are built) can be expected to preserve the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the information being processed, stored, or transmitted by the systems across the full range of threats”
  • Two factors affecting the trustworthiness of information systems are:
    • Security functionality: The security features/functions employed within the system. These include cryptographic and network security technologies
      • Security assurance: The grounds for confidence that the security functionality is effective in its application. This area is addressed by security management techniques, such as auditing and incorporating security considerations into the system development life cycle

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

SP 800-39 defines trustworthiness for information systems as the degree to which information systems (including the information technology products from which the systems are built) can be expected to preserve the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the information being processed, stored, or transmitted by the systems across the full range of threats. Two factors affecting the trustworthiness of information systems are: ■ Security functionality: The security features/functions employed within the system. These include cryptographic and network security technologies discussed throughout this book. ■ Security assurance: The grounds for confidence that the security functionality is effective in its application. This area is addressed by security management techniques, such as auditing and incorporating security considerations into the system development life cycle [STAL19].

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. SP 800-39 defines trustworthiness for information systems as “the degree to which information systems … can be expected to preserve the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the information … across the full range of threats”

    جدارة النظام بالثقة: مدى توقع أن يحافظ على CIA للمعلومات ضد كل أنواع التهديدات.

    System trustworthiness: how far a system can be expected to preserve CIA across the full range of threats.

  2. Security functionality: The security features/functions employed within the system. These include cryptographic and network security technologies

    الوظائف الأمنية: الميزات الأمنية في النظام (تشفير، أمن شبكات).

    Security functionality: the security features in the system (cryptography, network security).

  3. Security assurance: The grounds for confidence that the security functionality is effective in its application. … auditing and incorporating security considerations into the system development life cycle

    الضمان الأمني: الأسس التي تجعلنا واثقين أن هذه الوظائف فعالة فعلًا (التدقيق، ودمج الأمن في دورة تطوير النظام).

    Security assurance: the grounds for confidence that the functionality actually works (auditing, building security into the development life cycle).

الشرح — شرح موسّع

الوظائف = «ماذا يملك النظام من حماية»، والضمان = «كيف نتأكد أنها تعمل». نظام فيه تشفير لكن لم يُدقق قط لديه وظائف بلا ضمان.

Functionality = “what protection the system has”; assurance = “how we know it works”. A system with encryption that was never audited has functionality without assurance.

الخلاصة

جدارة النظام = الوظائف الأمنية + الضمان الأمني.
System trustworthiness = security functionality + security assurance.

الشريحة 37 — Establishing Trust Relationships

المصدر — المحتوى الأصلي

  • Validated trust:
  • Trust is based on evidence obtained by the trusting organization about the trusted organization or entity. The information may include information security policy, security measures, and level of oversight
  • Direct historical trust:
  • This type of trust is based on the security-related track record exhibited by an organization in the past, particularly in interactions with the organization seeking to establish trust
  • Mediated trust:
  • Mediated trust involves the use of a third party that is mutually trusted by two parties, with the third party providing assurance or guarantee of a given level of trust between the first two parties
  • Mandated trust:
  • An organization establishes a level of trust with another organization based on a specific mandate issued by a third party in a position of authority

© 2020 Pearson Education, Inc., Hoboken, NJ. All rights reserved.

📝 ملاحظات المحاضر في ملف الشرائح (المصدر)

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

The methods used by an organization to establish a trust relationship with various entities will depend on a variety of factors, such as laws and regulations, risk tolerance, and the criticality and sensitivity of the relationship. SP 800-39 describes the following methods: ■ Validated trust: Trust is based on evidence obtained by the trusting organization about the trusted organization or entity. The information may include information security policy, security measures, and level of oversight. An example for one organization to develop an application or information system and provides evidence (e.g., security plan, assessment results) to a second organization that supports the claims by the first organization that the application/system meets certain security requirements and/or addresses the appropriate security controls. ■ Direct historical trust: This type of trust is based on the security-related track record exhibited by an organization in the past, particularly in interactions with the organization seeking to establish trust. ■ Mediated trust: Mediated trust involves the use of a third party that is mutually trusted by two parties, with the third party providing assurance or guarantee of a given level of trust between the first two parties. An example of this form of trust establishment is the use of public-key certificate authorities, described in Chapter 14. ■ Mandated trust: An organization establishes a level of trust with another organization based on a specific mandate issued by a third party in a position of authority. For example, an organization may be given the responsibility and the authority to issue public key certificates for a group of organizations. An organization is likely to use a combination of these methods to establish relationships with a number of other entities.

الشرح — جملة بجملة

  1. Validated trust: Trust is based on evidence obtained by the trusting organization about the trusted organization or entity…

    الثقة المُتحقق منها: مبنية على أدلة تجمعها المنظمة عن الطرف الآخر (سياسته الأمنية، إجراءاته، مستوى الرقابة).

    Validated trust: based on evidence the trusting organization gathers (security policy, measures, oversight).

  2. Direct historical trust: … based on the security-related track record exhibited by an organization in the past…

    الثقة التاريخية المباشرة: مبنية على سجل الطرف الآخر الأمني في التعاملات السابقة.

    Direct historical trust: based on the other party's past security track record.

  3. Mediated trust: … the use of a third party that is mutually trusted by two parties…

    الثقة بالوساطة: طرف ثالث يثق به الطرفان يضمن مستوى الثقة بينهما.

    Mediated trust: a third party trusted by both vouches for the trust level between them.

  4. Mandated trust: … based on a specific mandate issued by a third party in a position of authority

    الثقة المفروضة: بأمر من جهة ذات سلطة (مثل جهة حكومية).

    Mandated trust: based on an order from an authority (e.g. a government body).

الشرح — شرح موسّع

أمثلة (إضافية): متحقق منها: تدقيق مزود قبل التعاقد. تاريخية: شريك تعاملت معه سنوات بلا حوادث. بالوساطة: سلطة الشهادات (CA) التي يثق بها المتصفح والموقع. مفروضة: جهة حكومية تلزم الوزارات بمزود معين.

Examples (additional): validated: auditing a provider before signing. Historical: a partner with years of incident-free dealings. Mediated: a certificate authority trusted by both browser and website. Mandated: a government body requiring ministries to use a specific provider.

الخلاصة

أربع طرق لبناء الثقة: متحقق منها، تاريخية مباشرة، بالوساطة، مفروضة.
Four ways to establish trust: validated, direct historical, mediated, mandated.

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Many of the security techniques and applications described in this book have been specified as standards. Additionally, standards have been developed to cover management practices and the overall architecture of security mechanisms and services. Throughout this book, we describe the most important standards in use or being developed for various aspects of cryptography and network security. Various organizations have been involved in the development or promotion of these standards. The most important (in the current context) of these organizations are as follows: ■ National Institute of Standards and Technology: NIST is a U.S. federal agency that deals with measurement science, standards, and technology related to U.S. government use and to the promotion of U.S. private-sector innovation. Despite its national scope, NIST Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) and Special Publications (SP) have a worldwide impact. ■ Internet Society: ISOC is a professional membership society with worldwide organizational and individual membership. It provides leadership in addressing issues that confront the future of the Internet and is the organization home for the groups responsible for Internet infrastructure standards, including the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) and the Internet Architecture Board (IAB). These organizations develop Internet standards and related specifications, all of which are published as Requests for Comments (RFCs). ■ ITU-T: The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) is an international organization within the United Nations System in which governments and the private sector coordinate global telecom networks and services. The ITU Telecommunication Standardization Sector (ITU-T) is one of the three sectors of the ITU. ITU-T’s mission is the development of technical standards covering all fields of telecommunications. ITU-T standards are referred to as Recommendations. ■ ISO: The International Organization for Standardization (ISO) is a worldwide federation of national standards bodies from more than 140 countries, one from each country. ISO is a nongovernmental organization that promotes the development of standardization and related activities with a view to facilitating the international exchange of goods and services and to developing cooperation in the spheres of intellectual, scientific, technological, and economic activity. ISO’s work results in international agreements that are published as International Standards.

المصدر — ملاحظات المتحدث

Figure 1.6, adapted from [MAYE95], illustrates the relationship among these concepts. Propensity can also be expressed as the level of risk that an entity (individual or organization) is prepared to tolerate. Typically, a trustor uses a number of factors to establish the trustworthiness of an entity. Three general factors are commonly cited: ■ Ability: Also referred to as competence, this relates to the potential ability of the evaluated entity to do a given task or be entrusted with given information. ■ Benevolence: This implies a disposition of goodwill towards the trusting party. That is, a trustworthy party does not intend to cause harm to the trusting party. ■ Integrity: This can be defined as the trustor’s perception that the trustee adheres to a set of principles that the trustor finds acceptable. Integrity implies that a benevolent party takes such measures are necessary to assure that it in fact does not cause harm to the trusting party. The goal of trust, in the model of Figure 1.6, is to determine what course of action, if any, the trusting party is willing to take in relation to the trusted party. Based on the level of trust, and the perceived risk, the trusting party may decide to take some action the involves some degree of risk taking. The outcome of the risk taking could be a reliance on the trusted party to perform some action or the disclosure of information to the trusted party with the expectation that the information will be protected as agreed between the parties.

Attack            Service                 Mechanism (example)
----------------  ----------------------  -------------------------
Release of msg    Data confidentiality    Encryption
Traffic analysis  Traffic-flow conf.      Traffic padding
Masquerade        Authentication          Authentication exchange
Replay            Data integrity (conn.)  Data integrity mechanisms
Modification      Data integrity          Digital signature / MAC
Denial of service Availability service    Access control, mgmt

05 ثلاثة مستويات

  • CIA مثل خزانة: السرية = لا أحد غيرك يرى ما فيها، السلامة = لا أحد يغيّر ما فيها، الإتاحة = تستطيع فتحها متى احتجت.
  • الهجوم السلبي مثل شخص يسترق السمع لمكالمتك؛ النشط مثل شخص يقطع المكالمة أو ينتحل صوتك.
  • الخدمة = ماذا نريد (مثلًا: لا أحد يقرأ رسالتي)، والآلية = كيف (التشفير).
  • بلا مفتاح: بصمة للرسالة. مفتاح واحد: نفس المفتاح للقفل والفتح. مفتاحان: مفتاح عام يقفل وخاص يفتح.
  • الجدار الناري حارس بوابة، IDS جرس إنذار، IPS حارس يوقف اللص.
  • الثقة: تثق بمن أثبت جدارته، أو بتاريخه معك، أو لأن طرفًا تثق به يضمنه، أو لأن جهة رسمية تفرضه.
  • CIA is like a locker: confidentiality = nobody else sees inside, integrity = nobody changes what's inside, availability = you can open it whenever you need.
  • A passive attack is someone listening in on your call; an active one cuts the call or imitates your voice.
  • A service is what we want (nobody reads my message); a mechanism is how (encryption).
  • Keyless: a fingerprint of a message. Single-key: the same key locks and unlocks. Two-key: a public key locks, a private key unlocks.
  • A firewall is a gate guard, IDS an alarm bell, IPS a guard who stops the thief.
  • Trust: you trust someone who proved themselves, has history with you, is vouched for by someone you trust, or is required by an authority.
  • الأهداف (X.800/FIPS): Confidentiality (data confidentiality, privacy)، Integrity (data integrity ⊇ authenticity, nonrepudiation؛ system integrity)، Availability؛ إضافة إلى Authenticity وAccountability (الشكل 1.1).
  • بنية OSI (X.800): Attack ← يواجهه Service ← تنفذه Mechanism(s). التهديد = احتمال خرق؛ الهجوم = فعل ذكي متعمد (RFC 4949).
  • الهجمات السلبية (release of message contents، traffic analysis) لا تغيّر الموارد ← المعالجة بالمنع. النشطة (masquerade، replay، modification، DoS) ← المعالجة بالكشف والتعافي.
  • الخدمات الست: authentication (peer entity، data origin)، access control، data confidentiality (+ traffic-flow)، data integrity (connection-oriented ضد duplication/insertion/modification/reordering/replay؛ connectionless ضد modification فقط)، nonrepudiation (origin وdestination)، availability.
  • الآليات الثماني؛ والتشفير reversible (encryption) أو irreversible (hash، MAC).
  • Keyless: hash، PRNG. Single-key: block (modes of operation تعتمد على الكتل السابقة)، stream، MAC. Two-key: asymmetric encryption، digital signature، key exchange، user authentication.
  • Trust: trustworthiness، propensity، risk = f(impact، likelihood)؛ trustworthiness of IS = security functionality + security assurance (SP 800-39)؛ validated / direct historical / mediated / mandated.
  • Objectives (X.800/FIPS): confidentiality (data confidentiality, privacy), integrity (data integrity ⊇ authenticity, nonrepudiation; system integrity), availability; plus authenticity and accountability (Figure 1.1).
  • OSI architecture (X.800): attack ← countered by service ← implemented by mechanism(s). Threat = potential violation; attack = deliberate intelligent act (RFC 4949).
  • Passive attacks (release of message contents, traffic analysis) don't alter resources → handled by prevention. Active (masquerade, replay, modification, DoS) → handled by detection and recovery.
  • Six services: authentication (peer entity, data origin), access control, data confidentiality (+ traffic flow), data integrity (connection-oriented vs duplication/insertion/modification/reordering/replay; connectionless vs modification only), nonrepudiation (origin and destination), availability.
  • Eight mechanisms; cryptographic ones reversible (encryption) or irreversible (hash, MAC).
  • Keyless: hash, PRNG. Single-key: block (modes depend on earlier blocks), stream, MAC. Two-key: asymmetric encryption, digital signature, key exchange, user authentication.
  • Trust: trustworthiness, propensity, risk = f(impact, likelihood); IS trustworthiness = security functionality + security assurance (SP 800-39); validated / direct historical / mediated / mandated.
  • CIA + Authenticity + Accountability = 5 أهداف.
  • السرية = سرية البيانات + الخصوصية.
  • السلامة = البيانات (+ أصالة، عدم إنكار) + النظام.
  • Attack / Service / Mechanism.
  • تهديد = احتمال؛ هجوم = فعل.
  • سلبي (2): كشف المحتوى، تحليل المرور ← منع.
  • نشط (4): انتحال، إعادة إرسال، تعديل، حجب خدمة ← كشف وتعافٍ.
  • 6 خدمات، 8 آليات.
  • Peer entity = اتصال؛ Data origin = بريد.
  • Integrity موجّهة بالاتصال: 5 حمايات؛ عديمة الاتصال: تعديل فقط.
  • بلا مفتاح 2، مفتاح واحد 3، مفتاحان 4.
  • MAC يتحقق منه حامل المفتاح؛ التوقيع يتحقق منه أي أحد.
  • Firewall يرشح، IDS ينبه، IPS يوقف.
  • ثقة: متحقق منها، تاريخية، بالوساطة، مفروضة.
  • CIA + authenticity + accountability = 5 objectives.
  • Confidentiality = data confidentiality + privacy.
  • Integrity = data (+ authenticity, nonrepudiation) + system.
  • Attack / service / mechanism.
  • Threat = potential; attack = act.
  • Passive (2): release of contents, traffic analysis → prevent.
  • Active (4): masquerade, replay, modification, DoS → detect and recover.
  • 6 services, 8 mechanisms.
  • Peer entity = connection; data origin = email.
  • Connection-oriented integrity: 5 protections; connectionless: modification only.
  • Keyless 2, single-key 3, two-key 4.
  • A MAC is verified by key holders; a signature by anyone.
  • Firewall filters, IDS alerts, IPS stops.
  • Trust: validated, historical, mediated, mandated.

06 اختبار تفاعلي

النتيجة 0/30

    07 نصائح احترافية

    كيف تفهم بدل أن تحفظ

    • ارسم الشكل 1.2 من ذاكرتك: 2 + 4 هجمات، 6 خدمات، 8 آليات.
    • لكل هجوم اسأل: ماذا يرى المهاجم؟ هل يرسل شيئًا؟ (الشكل 1.3)
    • اربط كل هجوم بخدمة ثم بآلية (جدول القسم 03).
    • قارن الأزواج المتشابهة: تهديد/هجوم، peer entity/data origin، MAC/توقيع، IDS/IPS.
    • أعطِ مثالًا من حياتك لكل نوع ثقة.
    • Draw Figure 1.2 from memory: 2 + 4 attacks, 6 services, 8 mechanisms.
    • For each attack ask: what does the attacker see? Do they send anything? (Figure 1.3)
    • Link every attack to a service and then a mechanism (table in section 03).
    • Compare look-alike pairs: threat/attack, peer entity/data origin, MAC/signature, IDS/IPS.
    • Give a real-life example of each kind of trust.

    تمارين عملية مقترحة

    1. صنّف 10 حوادث أمنية من الأخبار: سلبي/نشط، وأي نوع.
    2. لتطبيق بنكي: اكتب خدمة وآلية لكل هدف من CIA.
    3. افتح موقعًا بـ HTTPS وحدد أي عناصر الشكل 1.5 مستخدمة.
    4. اكتب سيناريو replay وكيف تكشفه خدمة سلامة موجّهة بالاتصال.
    1. Classify 10 security incidents from the news: passive/active and which type.
    2. For a banking app, write a service and mechanism for each CIA objective.
    3. Open an HTTPS site and identify which Figure 1.5 elements are in use.
    4. Write a replay scenario and how connection-oriented integrity detects it.

    أخطاء شائعة

    • اعتبار تحليل المرور هجومًا نشطًا؛ هو سلبي.
    • الظن أن التشفير يمنع تحليل المرور؛ يحتاج حشو المرور.
    • الخلط بين الخدمة (ماذا) والآلية (كيف).
    • اعتبار MAC خوارزمية بلا مفتاح لأنه يستخدم تجزئة؛ هو بمفتاح واحد.
    • نسخ عبارة الشريحة 28 «single key» للخوارزميات غير المتماثلة؛ هي مفتاحان.
    • القول إن data origin authentication تمنع التكرار؛ لا تمنعه.
    • الخلط بين IDS (ينبه) وIPS (يوقف).
    • Calling traffic analysis active; it is passive.
    • Thinking encryption stops traffic analysis; that needs traffic padding.
    • Mixing up service (what) and mechanism (how).
    • Calling MAC keyless because it uses a hash; it is single-key.
    • Copying slide 28's “single key” for asymmetric algorithms; they use two keys.
    • Saying data origin authentication prevents duplication; it doesn't.
    • Confusing IDS (alerts) and IPS (stops).
